title.zh: 卷三百三十二 列傳第二百二十 西域四
title.raw: 卷三百三十二 列傳第二百二十 西域四 Volume 332 Biographies 220: Western Regions 4

sentences.zh: 撒馬兒罕

translations.literal: Samarkand
translations.idiomatic: Samarkand

sentences.zh: 撒馬兒罕，即漢罽賓地，隋曰漕國，唐復名罽賓，皆通中國。

translations.literal: Samarkand is the land of Kapisa in Han times; in Sui it was called Caogu, and in Tang the name Kapisa was restored—all had contact with China.
translations.idiomatic: Samarkand was the region known to the Han as Kapisa; the Sui called it Caogu, and the Tang restored the name Kapisa. In every era it maintained ties with China.

sentences.zh: 元太祖蕩平西域，盡以諸王、駙馬為之君長，易前代國名以蒙古語，始有撒馬兒罕之名。

translations.literal: The Yuan founding emperor swept the Western Regions flat, appointing princes and imperial sons-in-law as rulers throughout, replacing former state names with Mongol terms—only then did the name Samarkand arise.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan founder pacified the Western Regions, he installed princes and imperial sons-in-law as local rulers and replaced the old country names with Mongol designations; it was then that the name Samarkand first appeared.

sentences.zh: 去嘉峪關九千六百里。

translations.literal: It is nine thousand six hundred li from Jiayu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: It lies nine thousand six hundred li from Jiayu Pass.

sentences.zh: 元末為之王者，駙馬帖木兒也。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, the one who ruled it was the imperial son-in-law Timur.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan dynasty, the ruler there was Timur, an imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，太祖欲通西域，屢遣使招諭，而遐方君長未有至者。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu reign, the founding emperor wished to open contact with the Western Regions and repeatedly sent envoys to summon and instruct, yet no distant lords came.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu era, the founding emperor sought contact with the Western Regions and sent envoys again and again to invite their rulers, but none of the distant chiefs came.

sentences.zh: 二十年九月，帖木兒首遣回回滿剌哈非思等來朝，貢馬十五，駝二。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the twentieth year, Timur for the first time sent the Muslims Manlaha Feisi and others to court, presenting fifteen horses and two camels.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of year twenty, Timur sent his first embassy—the Muslims Manlaha Feisi and others—bearing fifteen horses and two camels as tribute.

sentences.zh: 詔宴其使，賜白金十有八錠。

translations.literal: An edict ordered a banquet for the envoys and bestowed eighteen ingots of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: The court held a banquet for the envoys and granted them eighteen ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 自是頻歲貢馬駝。

translations.literal: From then on, horses and camels were presented in tribute year after year.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent horses and camels as tribute nearly every year.

sentences.zh: 二十五年兼貢絨六匹，青梭幅九匹，紅綠撒哈剌各二匹及鑌鐵刀劍、甲胄諸物。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year they also presented six bolts of woolen cloth, nine bolts of blue tabby, two bolts each of red and green saha-la, and wootz-steel swords, armor, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-five they added six bolts of woolen cloth, nine bolts of blue tabby weave, two bolts each of red and green saha-la fabric, along with wootz-steel blades, armor, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 而其國中回回又自驅馬抵涼州互市。

translations.literal: Moreover, Muslims within their state drove horses on their own to Liangzhou to trade at the frontier market.
translations.idiomatic: Muslims from their country also drove horses on their own to Liangzhou to trade at the border markets.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，令赴京鬻之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit this and ordered them to go to the capital to sell them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and ordered them to bring their horses to the capital to sell.

sentences.zh: 元時回回遍天下，及是居甘肅者尚多，詔守臣悉遣之，於是歸撒馬兒罕者千二百餘人。

translations.literal: In Yuan times Muslims were spread throughout the realm; at this time many still lived in Gansu, and an edict ordered the frontier officials to send them all away—thus more than twelve hundred returned to Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Yuan, Muslim communities had spread across the empire, and many still remained in Gansu. The emperor ordered local officials to send them home, and more than twelve hundred people returned to Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 二十七年八月，帖木兒貢馬二百。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the twenty-seventh year, Timur presented two hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of year twenty-seven, Timur sent two hundred horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 其表曰：「恭惟大明大皇帝受天明命，統一四海，仁德洪布，恩養庶類，萬國欣仰。

translations.literal: His memorial stated: 'Respectfully considering that the Great Emperor of the Great Ming received Heaven's clear mandate, unified the four seas, spread benevolence broadly, nourished the myriad kinds with grace, and all states rejoice and look up.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial read: 'We respectfully acknowledge that the Great Emperor of the Great Ming received Heaven's mandate, united the four seas, spread his benevolence far and wide, nurtured all living kinds, and won the joyful admiration of every realm.

sentences.zh: 咸知上天欲平治天下，特命皇帝出膺運數，為億兆之主。

translations.literal: All know that Heaven wished to pacify and govern the realm and specially commanded the emperor to assume the allotted destiny and become lord of the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: All know that Heaven wished to bring peace to the world and specially appointed the emperor to take up his destined role as sovereign over the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 光明廣大，昭若天鏡，無有遠近，鹹照臨之。

translations.literal: His radiance is vast and bright, clear as a heavenly mirror; none, near or far, fails to receive his illumination.
translations.idiomatic: His brilliance is vast and bright, clear as a mirror in the sky; none, whether near or far, escapes his gaze.

sentences.zh: 臣帖木兒僻在萬里之外，恭聞聖德寬大，超越萬古。

translations.literal: Your subject Timur, remote ten thousand li away, respectfully heard that the sage virtue is broad and surpasses all ages.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject Timur, dwelling ten thousand li away, has respectfully heard that your sage virtue is magnanimous beyond anything known in all ages.

sentences.zh: 自古所無之福，皇帝皆有之。

translations.literal: Blessings unknown since antiquity—the emperor possesses them all.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings never known since antiquity—the emperor possesses them all.

sentences.zh: 所未服之國，皇帝皆服之。

translations.literal: States not yet submitted—the emperor has submitted them all.
translations.idiomatic: States not yet brought to submission—the emperor has brought them all to submission.

sentences.zh: 遠方絕域，昏昧之地，皆清明之。

translations.literal: Distant lands and remote borders, places of darkness—all are made clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Distant lands and remote borders, places once shrouded in darkness—all have been brought into the light.

sentences.zh: 老者無不安樂，少者無不長遂，善者無不蒙福，惡者無不知懼。

translations.literal: The old lack no peace and joy, the young lack no growth and fulfillment, the good lack no blessing, and the wicked lack no fear.
translations.idiomatic: The aged know peace and contentment, the young grow to maturity, the virtuous receive blessings, and the wicked know fear.

sentences.zh: 今又特蒙施恩遠國，凡商賈之來中國者，使觀覽都邑、城池，富貴雄壯，如出昏暗之中，忽睹天日，何幸如之！

translations.literal: Now we are again specially favored with grace toward distant states; all merchants who come to China are allowed to view the capitals and cities, rich, noble, and mighty—as if emerging from darkness and suddenly beholding the sun and sky. What fortune could equal this!
translations.idiomatic: Now your grace has been extended anew to distant lands: merchants who come to China are shown the capital and its cities, rich and majestic beyond compare—as though stepping from darkness into daylight. What greater fortune could there be!

sentences.zh: 又承敕書恩撫勞問，使站驛相通，道路無壅，遠國之人鹹得其濟。

translations.literal: We have also received an imperial letter of gracious consolation and inquiry, with relay stations linked so that roads are unblocked and people of distant states all obtain relief.
translations.idiomatic: We have also received your gracious edict of consolation and inquiry, with relay stations linked so that the roads are clear and travelers from distant lands may all find their way.

sentences.zh: 欽仰聖心，如照世之杯，使臣心中豁然光明。

translations.literal: Reverently we look up to the sage heart, like the world-illuminating cup, so that this subject's heart is suddenly clear and bright.
translations.idiomatic: We revere your sage heart as one would the world-illuminating cup, and our hearts are suddenly filled with light.

sentences.zh: 臣國中部落，聞茲德音，歡舞感戴。

translations.literal: The tribes within my state, hearing this virtuous proclamation, dance for joy in grateful admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes of my realm, hearing this proclamation of virtue, dance for joy in grateful devotion.

sentences.zh: 臣無以報恩，惟仰天祝頌聖壽福祿，如天地永永無極。」

translations.literal: Your subject has no means to repay this grace and can only look to Heaven in prayer, wishing the sage longevity, fortune, and emolument as boundless as heaven and earth forever.'
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has no means to repay such grace and can only look to Heaven, praying that your sacred life, fortune, and blessings endure as endlessly as heaven and earth.'

sentences.zh: 照世杯者，其國舊傳有杯光明洞徹，照之可知世事，故云。

translations.literal: The world-illuminating cup: their state had an old tradition of a cup luminous and penetrating, by which one could know worldly affairs when gazing into it—hence the phrase.
translations.idiomatic: The 'world-illuminating cup' refers to an old tradition in their country of a cup so luminous and clear that gazing into it revealed the affairs of the world—hence the expression.

sentences.zh: 帝得表，嘉其有文。

translations.literal: The emperor received the memorial and praised its literary quality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received the memorial and commended its eloquence.

sentences.zh: 明年命給事中傅安等齎璽書、幣帛報之。

translations.literal: The next year he ordered the supervising secretary Fu An and others to carry an imperial letter and silks in reply.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he dispatched the supervising secretary Fu An and others with an imperial letter and silks in reply.

sentences.zh: 其貢馬，一歲再至，以千計，並賜賓鈔償之。

translations.literal: Their tribute horses came twice a year, numbering in the thousands, and guest notes were bestowed in compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute horses arrived twice yearly, numbering in the thousands, and the court paid for them with guest notes.

sentences.zh: 成祖踐阼，遣使敕諭其國。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu emperor ascended the throne, he sent envoys with an imperial edict to instruct their state.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, he sent envoys with an edict to their country.

sentences.zh: 永樂三年，傅安等尚未還，而朝廷聞帖木兒假道別失八里率兵東，敕甘肅總兵官宋晟儆備。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongle, Fu An and the others had not yet returned, but the court heard that Timur was marching east by way of Beshbalik and ordered the Gansu regional commander Song Sheng to take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year three, Fu An's party had not yet returned when the court learned that Timur was marching east through Beshbalik. The regional commander of Gansu, Song Sheng, was ordered to stand ready.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，安等還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year, An and the others returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year five, Fu An and his party returned.

sentences.zh: 初，安至其國被留，朝貢亦絕。

translations.literal: At first, when An reached their state he was detained, and tribute missions also ceased.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu An first reached their country he was detained, and tribute missions ceased as well.

sentences.zh: 尋令人導安遍曆諸國數萬里，以誇其國廣大。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they had someone guide An through various states for tens of thousands of li to boast of their state's vast extent.
translations.idiomatic: They then had guides lead Fu An on a tour of their dominions for tens of thousands of li, to display how vast their realm was.

sentences.zh: 至是帖木兒死，其孫哈裏嗣，乃遣使臣虎歹達等送安還，貢方物。

translations.literal: By then Timur had died and his grandson Khalil succeeded; he then sent the envoy Hudaida and others to escort An back and present local products.
translations.idiomatic: By then Timur had died and his grandson Khalil had succeeded. He sent the envoy Hudaida and others to escort Fu An home with local products as tribute.

sentences.zh: 帝厚賚其使，遣指揮白阿兒忻台等往祭故王，而賜新王及部落銀幣。

translations.literal: The emperor richly rewarded the envoys and dispatched the commander Bai A'erxintai and others to sacrifice to the late king, while bestowing silver and silks on the new king and the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor richly rewarded the envoys and sent the commander Bai A'erxintai and others to perform rites for the late king, granting silver and silks to the new king and his tribes.

sentences.zh: 其頭目沙裏奴兒丁等亦貢駝馬。

translations.literal: Their chieftains, including Shalinu'erdin, also presented camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftains, including Shalinu'erdin, also sent camels and horses as tribute.

sentences.zh: 命安等賜其王彩幣，與貢使偕行。

translations.literal: An and the others were ordered to bestow colored silks on their king and travel together with the tribute envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Fu An and his party were ordered to present colored silks to their king and return with the tribute envoys.

sentences.zh: 七年，安等還，王遣使隨入貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, An and the others returned, and the king sent envoys to accompany them in presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven, Fu An returned, and the king sent envoys to accompany him to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 自後，或比年，或間一歲，或三歲，輒入貢。

translations.literal: Afterward, sometimes every other year, sometimes at one-year intervals, sometimes every three years, they would present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they sent tribute every other year, every year, or every three years, as the case might be.

sentences.zh: 十三年遣使隨李達、陳誠等入貢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year they sent envoys to enter tribute together with Li Da, Chen Cheng, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen they sent envoys to court with Li Da, Chen Cheng, and their party.

sentences.zh: 暨辭歸，命誠及中官魯安偕往，賜其頭目兀魯伯等白銀、彩幣。

translations.literal: When they took leave to return, Cheng and the eunuch Lu An were ordered to go together and bestow silver and colored silks on their chieftains, including Ulubek.
translations.idiomatic: When they departed, Chen Cheng and the eunuch Lu An were sent with them to grant silver and colored silks to their chieftains, including Ulubek.

sentences.zh: 其國復遣使隨誠等入貢。

translations.literal: Their state again sent envoys to enter tribute with Cheng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Their country again sent envoys to court with Chen Cheng's party.

sentences.zh: 十八年復命誠及中官郭敬齎敕及彩幣報之。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Cheng and the eunuch Guo Jing were again ordered to carry an edict and colored silks in reply.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen, Chen Cheng and the eunuch Guo Jing were again dispatched with an edict and colored silks in reply.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年秋、冬，頭目兀魯伯米兒咱等遣使再入貢。

translations.literal: In the autumn and winter of the fifth year of Xuande, the chieftains Ulubek Mirza and others sent envoys to enter tribute again.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn and winter of Xuande year five, the chieftains Ulubek Mirza and others sent another tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 七年遣中官李貴等齎文綺、羅錦賜其國。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the eunuch Li Gui and others were sent bearing figured silks and brocades to bestow on their state.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven the eunuch Li Gui and others were sent with figured silks and brocades as gifts to their country.

sentences.zh: 正統四年貢良馬，色玄，蹄額皆白。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhengtong they presented fine horses, black in color, with hooves and foreheads all white.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong year four they sent fine horses, black with white hooves and foreheads.

sentences.zh: 帝愛之，命圖其像，賜名瑞ＤＯ，賞賚有加。

translations.literal: The emperor loved it, ordered its likeness painted, and bestowed the name Ruiju, 'Auspicious Colt' (the source graph is corrupt), with extra rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, ordered a portrait painted, and bestowed the name Auspicious Colt, with lavish rewards besides.

sentences.zh: 十年十月書諭其王兀魯伯曲烈幹曰：「王遠處西陲，恪修職貢，良足嘉尚。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year a letter instructed their king Ulubek Quliegan: 'The king is far on the western border yet diligently maintains tribute duties—truly worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year ten a letter was sent to their king Ulubek Quliegan: 'Though you dwell far on the western frontier, you have faithfully maintained your tribute obligations—conduct truly worthy of commendation.

sentences.zh: 使回，特賜王及王妻子彩幣表裏，示朕優待之意。」

translations.literal: When the envoys return, colored silks, outer and inner, are specially granted to the king and the king's wife and children, showing Our intent to treat them favorably.'
translations.idiomatic: On your envoys' return, We have specially granted colored silks, outer and inner garments, to you, your wife, and your children, as a sign of Our favor.'

sentences.zh: 別敕賜金玉器、龍首杖、細馬鞍及諸色織金文綺，官其使臣為指揮僉事。

translations.literal: A separate edict bestowed gold and jade vessels, a dragon-headed staff, fine horse saddles, and various brocaded figured silks with gold thread, and appointed their envoy to the office of assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: A separate edict granted gold and jade vessels, a dragon-headed staff, fine saddles, and brocaded figured silks in various colors, and appointed their envoy assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 成化中，其鎖魯檀阿黑麻三入貢。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign, their Sulṭān Aḥmad presented tribute three times.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua era, their ruler Sulṭān Aḥmad sent tribute three times.

sentences.zh: 十九年偕亦思罕酋長貢二獅，至肅州，其使者奏請大臣往迎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, together with the Yishihan chieftain, they presented two lions; when they reached Suzhou, their envoys memorialized requesting senior officials to go welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen, together with the Yishihan chieftain, they sent two lions as tribute. At Suzhou their envoys petitioned for senior officials to come and receive them.

sentences.zh: 職方郎中陸容言：「此無用之物，在郊廟不可為犧牲，在乘輿不可被驂服，宜勿受。」

translations.literal: Lu Rong, director in the Bureau of Operations, said: 'These are useless creatures; in the suburban altars they cannot serve as sacrificial victims, and for the imperial carriage they cannot serve as outriders—they should not be accepted.'
translations.idiomatic: Lu Rong, director in the Bureau of Operations, said: 'These creatures serve no useful purpose—they cannot be offered at the suburban altars, nor harnessed to the imperial carriage. They should not be accepted.'

sentences.zh: 禮官周洪謨等亦言往迎非禮，帝卒遣中使迎之。

translations.literal: The ritual officials Zhou Hongmo and others also said that going to welcome them was contrary to ritual, but the emperor ultimately sent eunuchs to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials Zhou Hongmo and others also argued that sending officials to welcome them violated propriety, but the emperor ultimately dispatched eunuchs to receive them.

sentences.zh: 獅日啖生羊二，醋、酐、蜜酪各二瓶。

translations.literal: Each lion daily consumed two live sheep, and two jars each of vinegar, fermented grain drink, and honeyed curds.
translations.idiomatic: Each lion consumed two live sheep daily, along with two jars each of vinegar, fermented grain drink, and honeyed curds.

sentences.zh: 養獅者，光祿日給酒饌。

translations.literal: Those who kept the lions received daily wine and food from the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: The lion keepers received daily provisions of wine and food from the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 帝既厚加賜賚，而其使者怕六灣以為輕，援永樂間例為請。

translations.literal: Although the emperor had richly rewarded them, their envoy Paliuwan thought it meager and cited the Yongle precedent in petition.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor had granted lavish rewards, their envoy Paliuwan considered them insufficient and petitioned by citing the Yongle precedent.

sentences.zh: 禮官議從正統四年例，加彩幣五表裏。

translations.literal: The ritual officials deliberated and followed the precedent of the fourth year of Zhengtong, adding five sets of colored silks, outer and inner.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials decided to follow the precedent of Zhengtong year four and add five sets of colored silks, outer and inner garments.

sentences.zh: 使者復以為輕，乃加正、副使各二表裏，從者半之，命中官韋洛、鴻臚署丞海濱送之還。

translations.literal: The envoys again thought it meager, so two sets each were added for the chief and deputy envoys, and half that for attendants; the eunuch Wei Luo and the Honglu assistant director Haibin were ordered to escort them back.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys again found the rewards insufficient, so two additional sets were granted to the chief and deputy envoys and half that to their attendants. The eunuch Wei Luo and the Honglu assistant director Haibin were ordered to escort them home.

sentences.zh: 其使者不由故道赴廣東，又多買良家女為妻妾，洛等不為禁止。

translations.literal: Their envoys did not take the original route to Guangdong and bought many daughters of respectable families as wives and concubines; Luo and the others did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys did not take the usual route to Guangdong and bought many respectable families' daughters as wives and concubines; Wei Luo and his party did nothing to stop them.

sentences.zh: 久之，洛上疏委罪於濱，濱坐下吏。

translations.literal: After a long time, Luo memorialized shifting blame onto Haibin, and Haibin was handed over to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually Wei Luo memorialized, shifting blame onto Haibin, who was handed over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 其使者請泛海至滿剌加市狻猊以獻，市舶中官韋眷主之，布政使陳選力陳不可，乃已。

translations.literal: Their envoys requested to cross the sea to Malacca to buy lions for presentation; the maritime-trade eunuch Wei Juan favored it, but the provincial administration commissioner Chen Xuan strongly argued against it, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys asked permission to sail to Malacca to buy lions for tribute. The maritime-trade eunuch Wei Juan supported the plan, but the provincial commissioner Chen Xuan strongly objected, and the proposal was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 弘治二年，其使由滿剌加至廣東，貢獅子、鸚鵡諸物，守臣以聞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Hongzhi, their envoys came from Malacca to Guangdong, presenting lions, parrots, and other goods; the frontier officials reported it.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year two, their envoys arrived in Guangdong via Malacca with lions, parrots, and other tribute, which the local officials reported to the court.

sentences.zh: 禮官耿裕等言：「南海非西域貢道，請卻之。」

translations.literal: The ritual officials Geng Yu and others said: 'The South Sea is not the tribute route of the Western Regions—please reject them.'
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials Geng Yu and others said: 'The South Sea is not the Western Regions' tribute route. We ask that they be turned away.'

sentences.zh: 禮科給事中韓鼎等亦言：「猙獰之獸，狎玩非宜，且騷擾道路，供費不貲，不可受。」

translations.literal: The supervising secretaries of the Ritual Section, Han Ding and others, also said: 'Fierce beasts are not fit to be kept for amusement; moreover they disturb the roads and the cost of provision is incalculable—they should not be accepted.'
translations.idiomatic: The supervising secretaries of the Ritual Section, Han Ding and others, also argued: 'Such fierce beasts are not fit for amusement, and they disturb the roads at incalculable cost. They should not be accepted.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「珍禽奇獸，朕不受獻，況來非正道，其即卻還。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Rare birds and strange beasts—We do not accept them as tribute, especially when they come by an improper route; send them back at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'We do not accept rare birds and strange beasts as tribute, especially when they arrive by an improper route. Send them back at once.

sentences.zh: 守臣違制宜罪，姑貸之。」

translations.literal: The frontier officials violated propriety and ought to be punished, but for now We pardon them.'
translations.idiomatic: The local officials violated protocol and deserve punishment, but for now We pardon them.'

sentences.zh: 禮官又言：「海道固不可開，然不宜絕之已甚，請薄犒其使，量以綺帛賜其王。」

translations.literal: The ritual officials again said: 'The sea route certainly should not be opened, yet it is not fitting to cut them off too severely—please give the envoys a modest reward and grant their king a measured gift of silks.'
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials added: 'The sea route must not be opened, yet we should not cut them off entirely. Grant the envoys a modest reward and send their king a measured gift of silks.'

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 明年又偕土魯番貢獅子及哈剌、虎剌諸獸，由甘肅入。

translations.literal: The next year they again joined Turfan in presenting lions and beasts such as hala and hula, entering by way of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they again joined Turfan in sending lions and beasts such as hala and hula, entering through Gansu.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中官傅德、總兵官周玉等先圖形奏聞，即遣人馳驛起送。

translations.literal: The garrison eunuch Fu De, regional commander Zhou Yu, and others first painted likenesses and memorialized; they immediately sent men by express relay to hurry the animals onward.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Fu De and regional commander Zhou Yu first sent painted likenesses in a memorial, then immediately dispatched men by express relay to hurry the animals to the capital.

sentences.zh: 獨巡按御史陳瑤論其糜費煩擾，請勿納。

translations.literal: Only the touring censor Chen Yao argued that the waste and disturbance were excessive and requested that they not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Only the touring censor Chen Yao argued that the expense and disruption were excessive and petitioned that they not be accepted.

sentences.zh: 禮官議如其言，量給犒賞，且言：「聖明在禦，屢卻貢獻，德等不能奉行德意，請罪之。」

translations.literal: The ritual officials deliberated in accord with his words, granting a measured reward, and also said: 'Under a sage and enlightened reign, tribute has repeatedly been declined; De and the others could not carry out the imperial intent—please punish them.'
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials agreed and granted a measured reward, adding: 'Under your sage reign, tribute has repeatedly been declined, yet De and his colleagues failed to carry out your intent. We ask that they be punished.'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「貢使既至，不必卻回，可但遣一二人詣京。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Since the tribute envoys have arrived, they need not be sent back; only one or two may be sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: 'Since the tribute envoys have arrived, they need not be turned back entirely—send only one or two to the capital.

sentences.zh: 獅子諸物，每獸日給一羊，不得妄費。

translations.literal: For the lions and other creatures, each beast is to be given one sheep daily—no wasteful expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: For the lions and other beasts, grant one sheep per animal daily, and permit no wasteful expenditure.

sentences.zh: 德等貸勿治。」

translations.literal: De and the others were pardoned and not prosecuted.'
translations.idiomatic: De and his colleagues were pardoned and not prosecuted.'

sentences.zh: 後至十二年始來貢。

translations.literal: Only in the twelfth year thereafter did they come to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Only twelve years later did they send tribute again.

sentences.zh: 明年復至。

translations.literal: The next year they came again.
translations.idiomatic: They came again the following year.

sentences.zh: 而正德中猶數至。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign they still came several times.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde era they still came on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，貢使又至。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, tribute envoys came again.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year two, tribute envoys arrived again.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「諸國使臣在途者遷延隔歲，在京者伺候同賞，光祿、郵傳供費不貲，宜示以期約。」

translations.literal: The ritual officials said: 'Envoys of various states on the road delay for years; those in the capital wait together for rewards—the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the postal service bear incalculable costs. A fixed schedule should be announced.'
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials said: 'Envoys from various states linger on the road for years, while those in the capital wait together for rewards, burdening the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the postal service with incalculable expense. A fixed schedule should be announced.

sentences.zh: 因列上禁制數事，從之。

translations.literal: They thereupon listed several prohibitory regulations, which were approved.
translations.idiomatic: They then listed several regulatory restrictions, which were approved.

sentences.zh: 十二年偕天方、土魯番入貢，稱王者至百餘人。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year they entered tribute together with Mecca and Turfan; those calling themselves kings numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve they came to court with Mecca and Turfan, and more than a hundred men styled themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 禮官夏言等論其非，請敕閣臣議所答。

translations.literal: The ritual officials Xia Yan and others discussed the impropriety and requested an edict for grand secretaries to deliberate on the reply.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials Xia Yan and others argued that this was improper and asked that the grand secretaries be ordered to deliberate on the appropriate response.

sentences.zh: 張孚敬等言：「西域諸王，疑出本國封授，或部落自相尊稱。

translations.literal: Zhang Fuling and others said: 'The various kings of the Western Regions are probably titles granted within their own states, or honorifics adopted among the tribes themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuling and others said: 'The various kings of the Western Regions are probably titles granted within their own countries, or honorifics adopted by the tribes themselves.

sentences.zh: 先年亦有至三四十人者，即據所稱答之。

translations.literal: In former years there were also as many as thirty or forty; we simply answered according to what they called themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years there were as many as thirty or forty; we simply addressed them by the titles they claimed.

sentences.zh: 若驟議裁革，恐人情觖望，乞更敕禮、兵二部詳議。」

translations.literal: If we suddenly deliberate on cutting and reforming, we fear popular sentiment will be disappointed; we beg that the Ministries of Rites and War be again ordered to deliberate in detail.'
translations.idiomatic: If we suddenly move to cut back these titles, we fear resentment; we ask that the Ministries of Rites and War be ordered to deliberate further.

sentences.zh: 於是言及樞臣王憲等謂：「西域稱王者，止土魯番、天方、撒馬兒罕。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xia Yan and the chief minister Wang Xian and others said: 'Among those in the Western Regions who style themselves kings, only Turfan, Mecca, and Samarkand do so.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yan and chief minister Wang Xian and others then said: 'Among the Western Regions, only Turfan, Mecca, and Samarkand have rulers who properly style themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 如日落諸國，稱名雖多，朝貢絕少。

translations.literal: As for the states of the Land of Sunset, though their titles are many, tribute missions are extremely few.
translations.idiomatic: As for the states of the Land of Sunset, though they bear many titles, they send tribute only rarely.

sentences.zh: 弘、正間，土魯番十三入貢，正德間，天方四入貢，稱王者率一人，多不過三人，余但稱頭目而已。

translations.literal: Between Hongzhi and Zhengde, Turfan presented tribute thirteen times; in Zhengde, Mecca four times—those styling themselves kings were generally one, at most no more than three; the rest called themselves only chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Hongzhi and Zhengde eras, Turfan sent tribute thirteen times and Mecca four times during Zhengde. Typically only one man styled himself king, never more than three; the rest called themselves merely chieftains.

sentences.zh: 至嘉靖二年、八年，天方多至六七人，土魯番至十一二人，撒馬兒罕至二十七人。

translations.literal: By the second and eighth years of Jiajing, Mecca had as many as six or seven, Turfan eleven or twelve, and Samarkand as many as twenty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: By Jiajing years two and eight, Mecca sent as many as six or seven self-styled kings, Turfan eleven or twelve, and Samarkand as many as twenty-seven.

sentences.zh: 孚敬等言三四十人者，並數三國爾。

translations.literal: When Fuling and others spoke of thirty or forty, they were counting all three states together.
translations.idiomatic: When Fuling spoke of thirty or forty, he was counting all three countries together.

sentences.zh: 今土魯番十五王，天方二十七王，撒馬兒罕五十三王，實前此所未有。

translations.literal: Now Turfan has fifteen kings, Mecca twenty-seven, and Samarkand fifty-three—truly unprecedented before this.
translations.idiomatic: Now Turfan claims fifteen kings, Mecca twenty-seven, and Samarkand fifty-three—numbers never seen before.

sentences.zh: 弘治時回賜敕書，止稱一王。

translations.literal: In Hongzhi times the return edict addressed only one king.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi era, return edicts addressed only one king.

sentences.zh: 若循撒馬兒罕往歲故事，類答王號，人與一敕，非所以尊中國制外蕃也。

translations.literal: If we follow Samarkand's precedent of recent years, answering each with a kingly title and giving each man an edict, that is not how to honor China and regulate the outer barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: If we follow Samarkand's recent precedent of answering every claimant with a royal title and granting each man an edict, we fail to uphold China's dignity and its regulation of foreign states.

sentences.zh: 蓋帝王之馭外蕃，固不拒其來，亦必限以制，其或名號僭差，言詞侮慢，則必正以大義，責其無禮。

translations.literal: For an emperor governing outer barbarians, he certainly does not reject their coming, yet he must also bound them with regulations; if titles overstep or words are insulting, he must set them right with great principle and reprove their lack of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: An emperor governing foreign states does not reject their coming, yet he must bound them with regulations. If their titles overstep propriety or their words are insulting, he must correct them with righteous principle and rebuke their lack of decorum.

sentences.zh: 今謂本國所封，何以不見故牘？

translations.literal: Now they claim titles granted within their own state—why do no old records appear?
translations.idiomatic: They claim these titles were granted within their own countries—why do no records of this appear in our archives?

sentences.zh: 謂部落自號，何以達之天朝？

translations.literal: They say the tribes style themselves [as kings]—how did this reach the Celestial Court?
translations.idiomatic: They claim these are titles their own tribes assumed—how did such claims come to the attention of the Celestial Court?

sentences.zh: 我概給以敕，而彼即據敕恣意往來，恐益擾郵傳，費供億，殫府庫以實溪壑，非計之得也。」

translations.literal: If we give edicts indiscriminately, they will wield those edicts to come and go at will, fearing it will further disturb the postal relays, consume supplies, exhaust the treasury to fill ravines and gullies—this is not a sound plan.'
translations.idiomatic: If we issue edicts to all alike, they will use them as licenses to travel freely back and forth, further burdening the courier routes, draining provisioning costs, and emptying the treasury to enrich private pockets. That is no sound policy.'

sentences.zh: 帝納其言，國止給一敕，且加詰讓，示以國無二王之義。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this advice; for each state only one edict was granted, and rebukes were added, showing the principle that a state cannot have two kings.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this advice. Each state received only a single edict, along with stern reproaches explaining the principle that a realm cannot acknowledge two sovereigns.

sentences.zh: 然諸蕃迄不從，十五年入貢復如故。

translations.literal: Yet the various fan states to the end did not comply; in the fifteenth year tribute came as before.
translations.idiomatic: The foreign states nonetheless refused to comply, and by the fifteenth year their tribute missions had resumed their former pattern.

sentences.zh: 甘肅巡撫趙載奏：「諸國稱王者至一百五十餘人，皆非本朝封爵，宜令改正，且定貢使名數。

translations.literal: Gansu grand coordinator Zhao Zai memorialized: The men styling themselves kings among the various states exceed one hundred fifty; none are fiefs conferred by our dynasty—they should be ordered to correct this, and the roster of tribute envoys should be fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu grand coordinator Zhao Zai memorialized: More than one hundred fifty men among the tributary states style themselves as kings, yet none hold titles granted by our court. They should be ordered to correct their usage, and the roster of tribute envoys should be fixed by regulation.

sentences.zh: 通事宜用漢人，毋專用色目人，致交通生釁。」

translations.literal: For communications and trade affairs Han people should be employed; do not exclusively use Semu people, lest liaison breed incidents.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreters and trade liaison should be Han Chinese; exclusive reliance on Semu personnel breeds collusion and provokes trouble.

sentences.zh: 部議從之。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry approved and implemented the proposal.

sentences.zh: 二十六年入貢，甘肅巡撫楊博請重定朝貢事宜，禮官復列數事行之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year they came to tribute; Gansu grand coordinator Yang Bo requested re-fixing tribute-court matters, and the ritual officials again listed several items and put them into practice.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute arrived in the twenty-sixth year, Gansu grand coordinator Yang Bo petitioned to reform tribute regulations, and the Board of Rites again issued a set of rules that were put into effect.

sentences.zh: 後入貢，迄萬曆中不絕。

translations.literal: Later tribute missions continued without cease through the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute missions continued thereafter without interruption through the Wanli era.

sentences.zh: 蓋番人善賈，貪中華互市，既入境，則一切飲食、道途之資，皆取之有司，雖定五年一貢，迄不肯遵，天朝亦莫能難也。

translations.literal: For the fan people are skilled merchants and covet Sino-barbarian mutual markets; once inside the borders, all food and drink and travel costs they take from the officials. Though a five-year-once tribute was fixed, to the end they would not comply, and the Celestial Court also could not constrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The peoples of the frontier were skilled traders eager for trade with China. Once inside the border, they drew all provisions for food, drink, and travel from local officials. Although tribute was fixed at once every five years, they refused to observe the schedule, and the court had no effective means to compel them.

sentences.zh: 其國東西三千餘里，地寬平，土壤膏腴。

translations.literal: Its state east and west exceeds three thousand li; the land is broad and level, the soil rich and fertile.
translations.idiomatic: The realm stretched more than three thousand li from east to west. The terrain was broad and level, the soil rich and fertile.

sentences.zh: 王所居城，廣十餘里，民居稠密。

translations.literal: The city where the king dwells is more than ten li in breadth; common dwellings are dense.
translations.idiomatic: The royal capital sprawled more than ten li across, with densely packed dwellings.

sentences.zh: 西南諸蕃之貨皆聚於此，號為富饒。

translations.literal: Goods of the various fan states of the southwest all gather here; it is styled affluent.
translations.idiomatic: Merchandise from the southwestern states converged there, earning it a reputation for wealth.

sentences.zh: 城東北有土屋，為拜天之所，規制精巧，柱皆青石，雕為花文，中設講經之堂。

translations.literal: Northeast of the city is an earthen hall, a place for worshipping Heaven; its design is refined and clever, pillars all blue stone carved with floral patterns, within is set a hall for expounding scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Northeast of the city stood an earthen mosque, their place of worship. It was finely built, with blue-stone pillars carved in floral designs and, at its center, a hall for preaching scripture.

sentences.zh: 用泥金書經，裹以羊皮。

translations.literal: Scriptures are written in clay gold and wrapped in sheepskin.
translations.idiomatic: The scriptures were written in gold ink and bound in sheepskin.

sentences.zh: 俗禁酒。

translations.literal: Custom forbids wine.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was prohibited by custom.

sentences.zh: 人物秀美，工巧過於哈烈，而風俗、土產多與之同。

translations.literal: People and things are refined and beautiful; craftsmanship surpasses Herat, while customs and local products mostly are the same as it.
translations.idiomatic: The people were handsome and their crafts surpassed those of Herat, though customs and products largely resembled those of Herat.

sentences.zh: 其旁近東有沙鹿海牙、達失幹、賽藍、養夷，西有渴石、迭裏迷諸部落，皆役屬焉。

translations.literal: Nearby to the east are Shahrukhiya, Tashkent, Sayram, and Yangi; to the west are Kesh, Termez, and various tribes—all are subordinate and subject to it.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby to the east lay Shahrukhiya, Tashkent, Sayram, and Yangi; to the west were Kesh, Termez, and other subordinate tribes, all under its dominion.

sentences.zh: 沙鹿海牙

translations.literal: Shahrukhiya
translations.idiomatic: Shahrukhiya

sentences.zh: 沙鹿海牙，西去撒馬兒罕五百餘里。

translations.literal: Shahrukhiya is more than five hundred li west of Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Shahrukhiya lies more than five hundred li west of Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 城居小岡上，西北臨河。

translations.literal: The city sits on a small hill, facing a river to the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood on a low hill, with a river to the northwest.

sentences.zh: 河名火站，水勢沖急，架浮梁以渡，亦有小舟。

translations.literal: The river is named Huozhan; the current is swift and rushing; floating bridges are set up to cross, and there are also small boats.
translations.idiomatic: The river was called the Huozhan. Its current ran swift and strong; travelers crossed on pontoon bridges, though small boats were also available.

sentences.zh: 南近山，人多依崖谷而居。

translations.literal: South are nearby mountains; most people dwell along cliffs and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains lay to the south, and most inhabitants lived along the cliff-lined valleys.

sentences.zh: 園林廣茂。

translations.literal: Gardens and groves are broad and lush.
translations.idiomatic: Gardens and orchards spread widely and grew luxuriantly.

sentences.zh: 西有大沙洲，可二百里。

translations.literal: To the west is a great sandy expanse, about two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: To the west stretched a great sandy waste some two hundred li across.

sentences.zh: 無水，間有之，鹹不可飲。

translations.literal: There is no water; occasionally some appears, but it is brackish and undrinkable.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh water was scarce; where water appeared it was brackish and undrinkable.

sentences.zh: 牛馬誤飲之，輒死。

translations.literal: If cattle and horses drink it by mistake, they promptly die.
translations.idiomatic: Cattle and horses that drank it by mistake died at once.

sentences.zh: 地生臭草，高尺余，葉如蓋，煮其液成膏，即阿魏。

translations.literal: The ground produces a foul-smelling grass, over a foot tall, leaves like umbrellas; boiling its liquid makes a paste—that is asafoetida.
translations.idiomatic: The ground bore a foul-smelling grass over a foot tall with umbrella-like leaves; boiling its sap yielded a paste known as asafoetida.

sentences.zh: 又有小草，高一二尺，叢生，秋深露凝，食之如蜜，煮為糖，番名達郎古賓。

translations.literal: There is also a small grass, one or two feet tall, growing in clusters; in deep autumn dew congeals on it, and eating it is like honey; boiled it becomes sugar—the fan name is dagangubin.
translations.idiomatic: Another low plant, one or two feet tall and growing in clusters, collected autumn dew that tasted sweet as honey when eaten; boiled down it became a sugar the locals called dagangubin.

sentences.zh: 永樂間，李達、陳誠使其地，其酋即遣使奉貢。

translations.literal: During Yongle, Li Da and Chen Cheng were sent to this place; its chief immediately sent envoys to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, Li Da and Chen Cheng were dispatched there, and the local chief promptly sent envoys bearing tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年命中官李貴齎敕諭其酋，賜金織文綺、彩幣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuande the court ordered eunuch Li Gui to carry an edict to instruct its chief, bestowing gold-woven brocades and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Xuande reign, the court sent the eunuch Li Gui with an imperial edict to its chief, granting gold-woven brocades and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 達失幹

translations.literal: Tashkent
translations.idiomatic: Tashkent

sentences.zh: 達失幹，西去撒馬兒罕七百餘里。

translations.literal: Tashkent is more than seven hundred li west of Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Tashkent lies more than seven hundred li west of Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 城居平原，週二里。

translations.literal: The city sits on a plain, about two li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood on the plain, about two li in circumference.

sentences.zh: 外多園林，饒果木。

translations.literal: Outside are many gardens, abundant in fruit trees.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the walls lay many gardens rich in fruit trees.

sentences.zh: 土宜五穀。

translations.literal: The soil suits the five grains.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was well suited to grain cultivation.

sentences.zh: 民居稠密。

translations.literal: Common dwellings are dense.
translations.idiomatic: Houses stood close together.

sentences.zh: 李達、陳誠、李貴之使，與沙鹿海牙同。

translations.literal: The missions of Li Da, Chen Cheng, and Li Gui were the same as for Shahrukhiya.
translations.idiomatic: The missions of Li Da, Chen Cheng, and Li Gui followed the same pattern as that to Shahrukhiya.

sentences.zh: 賽藍，在達失幹之東，西去撒馬兒罕千餘里。

translations.literal: Sayram lies east of Tashkent, more than a thousand li west of Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Sayram lay east of Tashkent, more than a thousand li west of Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 有城郭，週二三里。

translations.literal: It has walls and moats, two or three li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: It had walled defenses two or three li in circumference.

sentences.zh: 四面平曠，居人繁庶。

translations.literal: On all four sides the land is flat and open; inhabitants are numerous and prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: The land lay flat and open on every side, and the population was large and prosperous.

sentences.zh: 五穀茂殖，亦饒果木。

translations.literal: The five grains grow luxuriantly; fruit trees are also abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Grain grew abundantly, and fruit trees were plentiful as well.

sentences.zh: 夏秋間，草中生黑小蜘蛛。

translations.literal: Between summer and autumn, in the grass grow small black spiders.
translations.idiomatic: Between summer and autumn, small black spiders appeared in the grass.

sentences.zh: 人被螫，遍體痛不可耐，必以薄荷枝掃痛處，又用羊肝擦之，誦經一晝夜，痛方止，體膚盡蛻。

translations.literal: If a person is stung, pain spreads over the whole body unbearably; one must sweep the painful spot with mint branches, also rub with sheep liver, and recite scripture for a day and night before pain stops and the skin completely sloughs off.
translations.idiomatic: A human sting brought unbearable pain throughout the body. Sufferers had to brush the wound with mint branches, rub it with sheep liver, and recite scripture for a full day and night before the pain ceased and the skin peeled away entirely.

sentences.zh: 六畜被傷者多死。

translations.literal: Of the six domestic animals, many stung die.
translations.idiomatic: Most livestock stung by them died.

sentences.zh: 凡止宿，必擇近水地避之。

translations.literal: Whenever stopping for the night, one must choose ground near water to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers making camp had to choose sites near water to avoid them.

sentences.zh: 元太祖時，都元帥薛塔剌海從征賽藍諸國，以砲立功，即此地也。

translations.literal: In the time of the Yuan founding ancestor, supreme commander Xue Talahai followed the campaign against Sayram and the various states, achieving merit with cannon—that was this place.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Yuan founder, supreme commander Xue Talahai campaigned against Sayram and neighboring states and won distinction with artillery—this was that place.

sentences.zh: 陳誠、李貴之使，與諸國同。

translations.literal: The missions of Chen Cheng and Li Gui were the same as for the other states.
translations.idiomatic: The missions of Chen Cheng and Li Gui followed the same pattern as those to the other states.

sentences.zh: 養夷，在賽藍東三百六十里。

translations.literal: Yangi is three hundred sixty li east of Sayram.
translations.idiomatic: Yangi lay three hundred sixty li east of Sayram.

sentences.zh: 城居亂山間。

translations.literal: The city sits amid rugged mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood amid rugged mountains.

sentences.zh: 東北有大溪，西流入巨川。

translations.literal: To the northeast is a great stream flowing west into a mighty river.
translations.idiomatic: A great stream to the northeast flowed west into a major river.

sentences.zh: 行百里，多荒城。

translations.literal: Traveling a hundred li, there are many ruined cities.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred li along the route lay many abandoned cities.

sentences.zh: 蓋其地介別失八里、蒙古部落之間，數被侵擾。

translations.literal: For its land lies between Beshbalik and Mongol tribes, repeatedly suffering raids.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory lay between Beshbalik and the Mongol tribes and had suffered repeated raids.

sentences.zh: 以故人民散亡，止戍卒數百人居孤城，破廬頺垣，蕭然榛莽。

translations.literal: Therefore the people scattered and fled; only several hundred garrison troops remain in a lonely city, broken huts and crumbling walls, desolate among thorns and brush.
translations.idiomatic: The populace had therefore scattered; only a few hundred garrison troops remained in a lonely walled town amid ruined huts, collapsed walls, and desolate scrubland.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，陳誠至其地。

translations.literal: During Yongle, Chen Cheng reached this place.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, Chen Cheng visited the place.

sentences.zh: 渴石，在撒馬兒罕西南三百六十里。

translations.literal: Kesh is three hundred sixty li southwest of Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Kesh lay three hundred sixty li southwest of Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 城居大村，周十餘里。

translations.literal: The city sits in a great village cluster, over ten li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The city occupied a large settlement more than ten li in circumference.

sentences.zh: 宮室壯麗，堂以玉石為柱，牆壁窗牖盡飾金碧，綴琉璃。

translations.literal: Palaces and halls are grand and splendid; halls have jade and stone pillars; walls, windows, and lattice are all adorned with gold and azure, set with glazed tile.
translations.idiomatic: Its palaces and halls were magnificent, with jade and stone pillars in the main halls, walls and windows gilded and painted in azure, and glazed tiles set throughout.

sentences.zh: 其先，撒馬兒罕酋長駙馬帖木兒居之。

translations.literal: Formerly, the Samarkand chief Timur the imperial son-in-law dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Timur, the Samarkand ruler and Yuan imperial son-in-law, had once made his residence there.

sentences.zh: 城外皆水田。

translations.literal: Outside the walls are all paddy fields.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the walls lay nothing but irrigated paddies.

sentences.zh: 東南近山，多園林。

translations.literal: Southeast are nearby mountains, with many gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains rose nearby to the southeast, and gardens were numerous.

sentences.zh: 西行十餘里，饒奇木。

translations.literal: Traveling west more than ten li, rare trees are abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Some ten li west, rare trees grew in abundance.

sentences.zh: 又西三百里，大山屹立，中有石峽，兩崖如斧劈。

translations.literal: Another three hundred li west, great mountains stand towering; within is a stone gorge, both cliffs like axe-cleaving.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred li farther west, great mountains rose sheer, with a stone gorge between cliffs cut as if by an axe.

sentences.zh: 行二三里出峽口，有石門，色似鐵，路通東西，番人號為鐵門關，設兵守之。

translations.literal: Traveling two or three li one emerges from the gorge mouth; there is a stone gate, color like iron, the road connecting east and west; the fan people style it Iron Gate Pass, and troops are stationed to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: After two or three li one emerged from the gorge mouth onto a stone gate dark as iron, with a road running east and west. The locals called it Iron Gate Pass and posted troops to guard it.

sentences.zh: 或言元太祖至東印度鐵門關，遇一角獸，能人言，即此地也。

translations.literal: Some say when the Yuan founding ancestor reached the Iron Gate Pass of Eastern India he encountered a unicorn that could speak human words—that was this place.
translations.idiomatic: Some say that when the Yuan founder reached the Iron Gate Pass of eastern India and met a unicorn that spoke human language, it was this very place.

sentences.zh: 迭裏迷

translations.literal: Termez
translations.idiomatic: Termez

sentences.zh: 迭裏迷，在撒馬兒罕西南，去哈烈二千餘里。

translations.literal: Termez is southwest of Samarkand, more than two thousand li from Herat.
translations.idiomatic: Termez lay southwest of Samarkand, more than two thousand li from Herat.

sentences.zh: 有新舊二城，相去十餘里，其酋長居新城。

translations.literal: There are new and old two cities, about ten li apart; the chief dwells in the new city.
translations.idiomatic: It had old and new cities some ten li apart; the chief resided in the new town.

sentences.zh: 城內外居民僅數百家，畜牧蕃息。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the city inhabitants number only several hundred households; livestock breed in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the walls lived only a few hundred households, though livestock thrived.

sentences.zh: 城在阿術河東，多魚。

translations.literal: The city is east of the Ashu River; fish are abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood east of the Ashu River, where fish were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 河東地隸撒馬兒罕，西多蘆林，產獅子。

translations.literal: East of the river the land is subordinate to Samarkand; to the west are many reed marshes, producing lions.
translations.idiomatic: The land east of the river was subject to Samarkand; to the west lay extensive reed marshes where lions were found.

sentences.zh: 陳誠、李達嘗使其地。

translations.literal: Chen Cheng and Li Da were once sent to this place.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Cheng and Li Da were once dispatched there.

sentences.zh: 卜花兒

translations.literal: Bukhara
translations.idiomatic: Bukhara

sentences.zh: 卜花兒，在撒馬兒罕西北七百餘里。

translations.literal: Bukhara is more than seven hundred li northwest of Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Bukhara lay more than seven hundred li northwest of Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 城居平川，周十餘里，戶萬計。

translations.literal: The city sits on level plains, over ten li in circumference, households numbering ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood on level ground, more than ten li around, with households numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 市里繁華，號為富庶。

translations.literal: Market streets are bustling; it is styled affluent and prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Its markets were bustling, and it was renowned for wealth.

sentences.zh: 地卑下，節序嘗溫，宜五穀桑麻，多絲綿布帛，六畜亦饒。

translations.literal: The land is low-lying; seasons are often mild; suited to the five grains, mulberry, and hemp; silk floss, cotton cloth, and silks are abundant; the six domestic animals are also plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain was low-lying and the climate generally mild. Grain, mulberry, and hemp flourished; silk floss, cotton cloth, and silks were abundant, and livestock were plentiful.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年，陳誠自西域還，所經哈烈、撒馬兒罕、別失八里、俺都淮、八答黑商、迭裏迷、沙鹿海牙、賽藍、渴石、養夷、火州、柳城、土魯番、鹽澤、哈密、達失幹、卜花兒凡十七國，悉詳其山川、人物、風俗，為《使西域記》以獻，以故中國得考焉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yongle, Chen Cheng returned from the Western Regions, having passed through Herat, Samarkand, Beshbalik, Andahuai, Badakhshan, Termez, Shahrukhiya, Sayram, Kesh, Yangi, Huozhou, Liucheng, Turpan, Yanzhe, Hami, Tashkent, and Bukhara—in all seventeen states—and fully detailed their mountains and rivers, people and things, and customs, compiling Record of a Mission to the Western Regions to present; thus China was able to examine them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Yongle reign, Chen Cheng returned from the Western Regions having traveled through seventeen states—Herat, Samarkand, Beshbalik, Andahuai, Badakhshan, Termez, Shahrukhiya, Sayram, Kesh, Yangi, Huozhou, Liucheng, Turpan, Yanzhe, Hami, Tashkent, and Bukhara. He recorded their geography, peoples, and customs in a Record of a Mission to the Western Regions and presented it to the throne, enabling China to study them.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年命李達撫諭西域，卜花兒亦與焉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xuande Li Da was ordered to soothe and instruct the Western Regions; Bukhara was also among them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Xuande reign, Li Da was ordered to reassure and instruct the Western Regions; Bukhara was included among the states visited.

sentences.zh: 別失八里

translations.literal: Beshbalik
translations.idiomatic: Beshbalik

sentences.zh: 別失八里，西域大國也。

translations.literal: Beshbalik is a great state of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Beshbalik was a major power of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 南接于闐，北連瓦剌，西抵撒馬兒罕，東抵火州，東南距嘉峪關三千七百里。

translations.literal: South it adjoins Khotan, north connects to Oirat, west reaches Samarkand, east reaches Huozhou, southeast is three thousand seven hundred li from Jiayu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Khotan to the south and the Oirats to the north, reached Samarkand in the west and Huozhou in the east, and lay three thousand seven hundred li southeast of Jiayu Pass.

sentences.zh: 或曰焉耆，或曰龜茲。

translations.literal: Some call it Yanqi, some call it Kucha.
translations.idiomatic: Some identified it with Yanqi, others with Kucha.

sentences.zh: 元世祖時設宣慰司，尋改為元帥府，其後以諸王鎮之。

translations.literal: In the time of Yuan Shizu an pacification commission was established; soon it was changed to a marshal's headquarters; afterward princes were stationed to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kublai Khan an pacification commission was established, soon converted to a marshal's headquarters, and later princes were posted to govern the region.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，藍玉征沙漠，至捕魚兒海，獲撒馬兒罕商人數百。

translations.literal: During Hongwu, Lan Yu campaigned in the desert, reaching Buyur Lake, capturing several hundred Samarkand merchants.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign, Lan Yu campaigned into the desert as far as Buyur Lake and captured several hundred Samarkand merchants.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣官送之還，道經別失八里。

translations.literal: The founding ancestor sent officials to escort them back; on the road they passed through Beshbalik.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor sent officials to escort them home by way of Beshbalik.

sentences.zh: 其王黑的兒火者，即遣千戶哈馬力丁等來朝，貢馬及海青，以二十四年七月達京師。

translations.literal: Its king Khizr Khoja immediately sent chiliarch Hamaliding and others to court, presenting horses and sea eagles; they reached the capital in the seventh month of the twenty-fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: Its king, Khizr Khoja, promptly sent the chiliarch Hamaliding and others to court with horses and hunting falcons as tribute; they reached the capital in the seventh month of year twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，賜王彩幣十表裏，其使者皆有賜。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and granted the king ten lengths of colored silks inside and out; the envoys all received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and granted the king ten lengths of colored silks, inside and out; every envoy received gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 九月命主事寬徹、御史韓敬、評事唐鉦使西域。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he ordered senior clerk Kuanchi, censor Han Jing, and reviewer Tang Zheng as envoys to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he appointed the senior clerk Kuanchi, Censor Han Jing, and Reviewer Tang Zheng as envoys to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 以書諭黑的兒火者曰：「朕觀普天之下，後土之上，有國者莫知其幾。

translations.literal: A letter instructed Khizr Khoja, saying: I observe under all Heaven, upon the broad earth, how many states there are none can know.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a letter instructing Khizr Khoja: I look upon all under Heaven and the broad earth, and none can count how many states there are.

sentences.zh: 雖限山隔海，風殊俗異，然好惡之情，血氣之類，未嘗異也。

translations.literal: Though mountains limit and seas divide, winds differ and customs vary, yet feelings of liking and disliking, types of blood and breath, have never differed.
translations.idiomatic: Though mountains and seas divide them and winds and customs differ, the feelings of liking and disliking and the nature of living beings have never truly differed.

sentences.zh: 皇天眷佑，惟一視之。

translations.literal: August Heaven favors and protects, viewing all as one.
translations.idiomatic: August Heaven favors and protects all alike, viewing them as one.

sentences.zh: 故受天命為天下主者，上奉天道，一視同仁，俾巨細諸國，殊方異類之君民，鹹躋乎仁壽。

translations.literal: Therefore one who receives Heaven's mandate as ruler of all under Heaven, above serves the Way of Heaven, treating all with one kindness, causing great and small states, rulers and people of strange regions and different kinds, all to ascend to benevolence and longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore whoever receives Heaven's mandate to rule all under Heaven serves the Way of Heaven above and treats all with equal kindness, so that great and small states alike, and rulers and peoples of every distant land and alien kind, may attain benevolence and long life.

sentences.zh: 而友邦遠國，順天事大，以保國安民，皇天監之，亦克昌焉。

translations.literal: Friendly states and distant countries, obeying Heaven and serving the great, thereby preserving state and pacifying people—August Heaven oversees this, and they also can flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Friendly states and distant countries that obey Heaven and serve the great power thereby secure their realms and their people; August Heaven watches over them, and they too may flourish.

sentences.zh: 曩者我中國宋君，奢縱怠荒，奸臣亂政。

translations.literal: Formerly our China's Song ruler was extravagant, dissolute, negligent, and wasteful; treacherous ministers threw government into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Song rulers of our China grew extravagant, dissolute, and negligent, while treacherous ministers threw the government into disorder.

sentences.zh: 天監否德，於是命元世祖肇基朔漠，入統中華，生民賴以安靖七十餘年。

translations.literal: Heaven observed this lacking virtue and therefore commanded the Yuan founding ancestor to establish his base in the northern desert and enter to rule the Central Realm; the living people relied on this for peace and quiet for more than seventy years.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven observed this want of virtue and commanded the Yuan founder to establish his base in the northern steppe and rule the Central Realm, upon which the people enjoyed peace for more than seventy years.

sentences.zh: 至於後嗣，不修國政，任用非人，致幻綱盡弛，強陵弱，眾暴寡，民生嗟怨，上達於天。

translations.literal: As for the later descendants, they did not cultivate state affairs, employed unfit men, causing the bonds of law to slacken entirely; the strong bullied the weak, the many oppressed the few; people's lives sighed in resentment, reaching up to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: But their later descendants neglected statecraft and appointed unworthy men, until governance collapsed entirely: the strong oppressed the weak and the many tyrannized the few, and the people's grievances rose to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天用是革其命，屬之於朕。

translations.literal: Heaven used this to change its mandate and entrusted it to me.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven therefore changed the mandate and entrusted it to me.

sentences.zh: 朕躬握乾符，以主黔黎。

translations.literal: I personally grasp the seals of Qian and rule the black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: I myself hold the mandate of Heaven and rule the black-haired people.

sentences.zh: 凡諸亂雄擅聲教違朕命者兵偃之，順朕命者德撫之。

translations.literal: All disorderly heroes who monopolize culture and education and defy my command—by arms I quell them; those who obey my command—by virtue I soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: All rebellious warlords who monopolize authority and defy my command I shall subdue by force; those who obey my command I shall comfort with virtue.

sentences.zh: 是以三十年間，諸夏奠安，外蕃賓服。

translations.literal: Therefore within thirty years, all Xia was settled and secure, outer fan submitted in guest-service.
translations.idiomatic: Thus within thirty years the civilized lands were settled and secure, and the outer dominions submitted in tribute.

sentences.zh: 惟元臣蠻子哈剌章等尚率殘眾，生釁寇邊，興師致討，勢不容已。

translations.literal: Only Yuan minister Manzi Hala Zhang and others still led remnant hosts, giving rise to provocation and raiding the borders; to raise troops and proceed to punishment, the situation could not but continue.
translations.idiomatic: Only the former Yuan minister Manzi Hala Zhang and his fellows still led remnant bands, stirring trouble and raiding the frontier, so that military action became unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 兵至捕魚兒海，故元諸王、駙馬率其部屬來降。

translations.literal: When troops reached Buyur Lake, former Yuan princes and imperial sons-in-law led their dependents to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Buyur Lake, the former Yuan princes and imperial sons-in-law brought their followers in submission.

sentences.zh: 有撒馬兒罕數百人以貿易來者，朕命官護歸已三年矣。

translations.literal: There were several hundred people of Samarkand who had come for trade; I ordered officials to escort them home—already three years.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred Samarkand merchants who had come to trade had been under official escort on their return journey for three years already.

sentences.zh: 使者還，王即遣使來貢，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, the king immediately sent envoys to offer tribute; I greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys returned, you promptly sent tribute envoys, and I was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 王其益堅事大之誠，通好往來，使命不絕，豈不保封國于悠久乎？

translations.literal: May the king further strengthen sincerity in serving the great, friendly passage back and forth, missions unceasing—would this not preserve the enfeoffed state in long duration?
translations.idiomatic: Strengthen your devotion to serving the great power, maintain friendly exchanges, and let envoys pass unceasingly—will you not thereby secure your realm for generations?

sentences.zh: 特遣官勞嘉，其悉朕意。」

translations.literal: Specially dispatching officials to console and praise; fully understand my intent.
translations.idiomatic: I have specially dispatched officials to convey my commendation; understand my intentions fully.

sentences.zh: 徹等既至，王以其無厚賜，拘留之。

translations.literal: When Che and the others arrived, the king because they had no lavish gifts detained them.
translations.idiomatic: When Kuanchi and his party arrived, the king, finding their gifts insufficient, detained them.

sentences.zh: 敬、鉦二人得還。

translations.literal: Jing and Zheng, two men, were able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jing and Tang Zheng alone were allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 三十年正月復遣官齎書諭之曰：「朕即位以來，西方諸商來我中國互市者，邊將未嘗阻絕。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, first month, again dispatching officials bearing a letter to instruct, saying: Since I ascended the throne, western merchants who come to our China for mutual market—frontier generals have never blocked or cut off.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, first month, he again sent officials with a letter of instruction: Since my accession, frontier commanders have never hindered Western merchants coming to trade in China.

sentences.zh: 朕復敕吏民善遇之，由是商人獲利，疆埸無擾，是我中華大有惠于爾國也。

translations.literal: I also ordered officials and people to treat them well; thereby merchants obtained profit and the borderlands were undisturbed—this is our Central Realm having great benefit toward your state.
translations.idiomatic: I also commanded officials and commoners to treat them kindly, so that merchants profited and the border was untroubled—thus has China greatly benefited your country.

sentences.zh: 前遣寬徹等往爾諸國通好，何故至今不返？

translations.literal: Previously I sent Kuanchi and others to your various states to open friendship—why have they not yet returned?
translations.idiomatic: I previously sent Kuanchi and his companions to your lands to establish goodwill—why have they still not returned?

sentences.zh: 吾于諸國，未嘗拘留一人，而爾顧拘留吾使，豈理也哉！

translations.literal: I toward various states have never detained a single person, yet you moreover detain my envoys—is this reason!
translations.idiomatic: I have never detained anyone from any state, yet you detain my envoys—how can this be reasonable!

sentences.zh: 是以近年回回入境者，亦令於中國互市，待徹歸放還。

translations.literal: Therefore in recent years those of the Huihui who entered the borders, I also allowed them to mutual market in China, waiting until Che returned then releasing and sending back.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in recent years I have even permitted Muslim traders who entered the realm to trade in China, intending to release them when Kuanchi returns.

sentences.zh: 後諸人言有父母妻子，吾念其至情，悉縱遣之。

translations.literal: Later the various people said they had fathers, mothers, wives, and children; remembering their utmost feeling, I entirely released and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: Later they spoke of parents, wives, and children; moved by their deep attachment, I released them all.

sentences.zh: 今復使使諭爾，俾知朝廷恩意，毋梗塞道路，致啟兵端。

translations.literal: Now again sending envoys to instruct you, causing you to know the court's gracious intent—do not obstruct and block the roads, causing arms to be raised.
translations.idiomatic: I now send envoys again to make known the court's goodwill: do not block the roads and provoke war.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『怨不在大，亦不在小。

translations.literal: The Book says: Whether resentment lies in the great, it also does not lie in the small.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: Whether the grievance is great or small,

sentences.zh: 惠不惠，懋不懋。』

translations.literal: Whether kindness—kindness or not; whether earnest exertion—exertion or not.
translations.idiomatic: whether kindness is shown, whether earnest effort is made.

sentences.zh: 爾其惠且懋哉。」

translations.literal: You must be kind and earnest!
translations.idiomatic: You must be kind and earnest!

sentences.zh: 徹乃得還。

translations.literal: Che thereupon was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Only then was Kuanchi allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位之冬，遣官齎璽書彩幣使其國。

translations.literal: In the winter when Chengzu ascended the throne, he dispatched officials bearing a sealed edict and colored silks to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the Yongle emperor's accession, he sent envoys with a sealed edict and colored silks to Beshbalik.

sentences.zh: 未幾，黑的兒火者卒，子沙迷查幹嗣。

translations.literal: Before long Khizr Khoja died; his son Shamsh Khan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Khizr Khoja died, and his son Shamsh Khan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年遣使貢玉璞、名馬，宴賚有加。

translations.literal: In Yongle year two he sent envoys to offer jade rough and famous horses; feasting and gifts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongle he sent envoys bearing jade rough and fine horses; the court feasted them and granted extra rewards.

sentences.zh: 時哈密忠順王安克帖木兒為可汗鬼力赤毒死，沙迷查幹率師討之。

translations.literal: At that time Hami's Loyal and Obedient King Anketmur had been poisoned to death by the khan Guilichi; Shamsh Khan led troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Anketmur, the Loyal and Obedient King of Hami, had been poisoned by the khan Guilichi; Shamsh Khan led an army against him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其義，遣使賚以彩幣，令與嗣忠順王脫脫敦睦。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his righteousness, sent envoys bearing colored silks, and ordered him to be friendly with the succeeding Loyal and Obedient King Toto.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his conduct, sent envoys with colored silks, and instructed him to live in harmony with Toto, the new Loyal and Obedient King of Hami.

sentences.zh: 四年夏來貢，命鴻臚寺丞劉帖木兒齎敕幣勞賜，與其使者偕行。

translations.literal: In summer of year four he came to offer tribute; the emperor ordered Honglu Temple vice director Liu Timur to carry an edict and silks to console and grant, traveling together with their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of year four he sent tribute; the emperor ordered Liu Timur, vice director of the Court of State Ceremonial, to carry an edict and silks as rewards and to return with the envoys.

sentences.zh: 秋、冬暨明年夏，三入貢，因言撒馬兒罕本其先世故地，請以兵復之。

translations.literal: Autumn, winter, and the next year's summer—three times entering tribute; he moreover said Samarkand was originally his ancestors' old land and requested troops to recover it.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, winter, and the following summer he sent tribute three times, stating that Samarkand was his ancestors' former domain and asking for troops to recover it.

sentences.zh: 命中官把太、李達及劉帖木兒齎敕戒以審度而行，毋輕舉，因賜之彩幣。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered eunuchs Batai and Li Da and Liu Timur to carry an edict warning him to act after careful deliberation and not act lightly, and granted him colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the eunuchs Batai and Li Da, together with Liu Timur, to carry an edict warning him to weigh his actions carefully and not act rashly, and granted him colored silks.

sentences.zh: 六年，太等還，言沙迷查幹已卒，弟馬哈麻嗣。

translations.literal: In year six, Tai and the others returned, reporting that Shamsh Khan had already died and his younger brother Mahmud succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In year six, Batai and his party returned with word that Shamsh Khan had died and his younger brother Mahmud had succeeded.

sentences.zh: 帝即命太等往祭，並賜其新王。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered Tai and the others to go offer sacrifice and also bestow gifts on the new king.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once ordered Batai and his companions to perform the mourning rites and to bestow gifts on the new ruler.

sentences.zh: 八年以朝使往撒馬兒罕者，馬哈麻待之厚，遣使齎彩幣賜之。

translations.literal: In year eight, because court envoys going to Samarkand were treated generously by Mahmud, the emperor sent envoys bearing colored silks to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight, because Mahmud had treated court envoys bound for Samarkand with great hospitality, the emperor sent envoys with colored silks in reward.

sentences.zh: 明年貢名馬、文豹，命給事中傅安送其使還，賚金織文綺。

translations.literal: The next year he offered famous horses and patterned leopards; the emperor ordered supervising secretary Fu An to escort their envoys back and granted gold-woven patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent famous horses and snow leopards; the emperor ordered Fu An, supervising secretary of the Office of Scrutiny, to escort the envoys home and granted gold-woven brocades.

sentences.zh: 時瓦剌使者言馬哈麻將襲其部落，因諭以順天保境之義。

translations.literal: At that time Oirat envoys said Mahmud was about to attack their tribes; the emperor therefore instructed him in the meaning of obeying Heaven and preserving borders.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Oirat envoys reported that Mahmud was about to attack their tribes; the emperor therefore admonished him to obey Heaven and keep within his borders.

sentences.zh: 十一年，貢使將至甘肅，命所司宴勞，且敕總兵官李彬善遇之。

translations.literal: In year eleven, tribute envoys were about to reach Gansu; the emperor ordered the responsible offices to feast and console them, and also instructed regional commander Li Bin to treat them well.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven, when tribute envoys were approaching Gansu, he ordered the local authorities to entertain them and instructed the regional commander Li Bin to treat them hospitably.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，有自西域還者，言馬哈麻母及弟相繼卒。

translations.literal: The next winter, someone returning from the Western Regions reported that Mahmud's mother and younger brother had died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter a traveler returned from the Western Regions with word that Mahmud's mother and younger brother had died in succession.

sentences.zh: 帝湣之，命安齎敕慰問，賚以彩幣。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied this and ordered An to carry an edict of consolation and inquiry, granting colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved to pity and ordered Fu An to carry an edict of condolence with colored silks as gifts.

sentences.zh: 已而馬哈麻亦卒，無子，從子納黑失只罕嗣。

translations.literal: Before long Mahmud also died, without a son; his nephew Naghach Khan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Mahmud also died without an heir, and his nephew Naghach Khan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 十四年春，使來告喪。

translations.literal: In spring of year fourteen, envoys came to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year fourteen envoys came to announce his death.

sentences.zh: 命安及中官李達弔祭，即封其嗣子為王，賚文綺、弓刀、甲胄，其母亦有賜。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered An and eunuch Li Da to offer mourning sacrifice, immediately enfeoffing the successor son as king, granting patterned silks, bows, knives, and armor; his mother also received gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Fu An and the eunuch Li Da to perform mourning rites, enfeoffed the successor as king, and granted patterned silks, bows, knives, and armor; his mother received gifts as well.

sentences.zh: 明年遣使來貢，言將嫁女撒馬兒罕，請以馬市妝奩。

translations.literal: The next year he sent envoys to offer tribute, saying he would marry his daughter in Samarkand and requesting horses to purchase her dowry.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he sent tribute envoys, saying he would marry his daughter in Samarkand and asking permission to trade horses for her dowry.

sentences.zh: 命中官李信等以綺、帛各五百匹助之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered eunuchs Li Xin and others to assist with five hundred bolts each of patterned silk and plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the eunuch Li Xin and others to assist with five hundred bolts each of brocade and plain silk.

sentences.zh: 十六年，貢使速哥言其王為從弟歪思所弑，而自立，徙其部落西去，更國號曰亦力把裏。

translations.literal: In year sixteen, tribute envoy Suke reported that their king had been murdered by his younger cousin Wais, who then established himself, moved their tribes westward, and changed the state name to Yilibali.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen the tribute envoy Suke reported that their king had been murdered by his cousin Wais, who seized power, moved the tribes westward, and renamed the state Yilibali.

sentences.zh: 帝以番俗不足治，授速哥為都督僉事，而遣中官楊忠等賜歪思弓刀、甲胄及文綺、彩幣，其頭目忽歹達等七十餘人並有賜，自是奉貢不絕。
