translations.literal: The emperor, considering fan customs not worth governing, appointed Suke as assistant regional commander, and sent eunuchs Yang Zhong and others to grant Wais bows, knives, armor, patterned silks, and colored silks; chieftains Hudaida and more than seventy others all received gifts—from this tribute offerings were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, deeming the frontier customs beyond full regulation, appointed Suke assistant regional commander and sent the eunuch Yang Zhong and others to grant Wais bows, knives, armor, brocades, and colored silks; more than seventy chieftains including Hudaida received gifts as well, and from then on tribute never ceased.

sentences.zh: 其國無城郭宮室，隨水草畜牧。

translations.literal: Their state had no walls, cities, or palaces; they followed water and grass in herding livestock.
translations.idiomatic: The country had no walled cities or palaces; the people followed pasture and water in nomadic herding.

sentences.zh: 人性獷悍，君臣上下無體統。

translations.literal: Human nature was fierce and violent; ruler and minister, superior and inferior, had no ritual order.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fierce by nature, and no proper order obtained between ruler and subject.

sentences.zh: 飲食衣服多與瓦剌同。

translations.literal: Food, drink, and clothing mostly were the same as the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: Their food, drink, and dress largely resembled those of the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 地極寒，深山窮穀，六月亦飛雪。

translations.literal: The land was extremely cold; in deep mountains and remote valleys, even in the sixth month snow flew.
translations.idiomatic: The land was bitterly cold; in its deep mountains and remote valleys snow fell even in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 哈烈，一名黑魯，在撒馬兒罕西南三千里，去嘉峪關萬二千餘里，西域大國也。

translations.literal: Herat, also called Heilu, lies three thousand li southwest of Samarkand, more than twelve thousand li from Jiayu Pass—a great state of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Herat, also known as Heilu, lay three thousand li southwest of Samarkand and more than twelve thousand li from Jiayu Pass; it was a major power of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 元駙馬帖木兒既君撒馬兒罕，又遣其子沙哈魯據哈烈。

translations.literal: The Yuan imperial son-in-law Timur, having become lord of Samarkand, also sent his son Shahrukh to hold Herat.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuan imperial son-in-law Timur became ruler of Samarkand, he sent his son Shahrukh to hold Herat.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，撒馬兒罕及別失八里咸朝貢，哈烈道遠不至。

translations.literal: During Hongwu, Samarkand and Beshbalik both came to court with tribute; Herat, the road being distant, did not come.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign, Samarkand and Beshbalik both sent tribute, but Herat, being so remote, did not.

sentences.zh: 二十五年遣官詔諭其王，賜文綺、彩幣，猶不至。

translations.literal: In year twenty-five he dispatched officials with an edict to instruct their king and granted patterned silks and colored silks; still they did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-five he sent officials with an edict to their king and granted brocades and colored silks, yet they still did not come.

sentences.zh: 二十八年遣給事中傅安、郭驥等攜士卒千五百人往，為撒馬兒罕所留，不得達。

translations.literal: In year twenty-eight he sent supervising secretaries Fu An, Guo Ji, and others, taking one thousand five hundred soldiers; they were detained by Samarkand and could not reach there.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight he sent Fu An and Guo Ji, supervising secretaries, with fifteen hundred soldiers, but Samarkand detained them and they never reached Herat.

sentences.zh: 三十年又遣北平按察使陳德文等往，亦久不還。

translations.literal: In year thirty he again sent Beiping surveillance commissioner Chen Dewen and others; they too long did not return.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty he again sent Chen Dewen, surveillance commissioner of Beiping, and others, who likewise did not return for a long time.

sentences.zh: 成祖踐阼，遣官齎璽書彩幣賜其王，猶不報命。

translations.literal: When Chengzu ascended the throne, he sent officials bearing a sealed edict and colored silks to grant their king; still no reply was reported.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle emperor took the throne, he sent officials with a sealed edict and colored silks to their king, yet still received no response.

sentences.zh: 永樂五年，安等還。

translations.literal: In Yongle year five, An and the others returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yongle, Fu An and his party returned.

sentences.zh: 德文遍曆諸國，說其酋長入貢，皆以道遠無至者，亦於是年始還。

translations.literal: Dewen traveled through all the states, persuading their chieftains to enter tribute; all said the road was distant and none came; he also only in that year first returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Dewen traveled through many states urging their chieftains to send tribute, but none came, citing the distance; he too returned only in that year.

sentences.zh: 德文，保昌人，采諸方風俗作為歌詩以獻。

translations.literal: Dewen, a native of Baochang, gathered customs of various regions and composed them as songs and poems to present.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen, a native of Baochang, collected the customs of many regions and composed songs and poems to present at court.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，擢僉都御史。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and promoted him to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 明年復遣安齎書幣往哈烈，其酋沙哈魯把都兒遣使隨安朝貢。

translations.literal: The next year he again sent An bearing a letter and silks to Herat; its chieftain Shahrukh Batur dispatched envoys to follow An in court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again sent Fu An with a letter and silks to Herat; the chieftain Shahrukh Batur sent envoys to accompany him to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 七年達京師，復命齎賜物偕其使往報。

translations.literal: In year seven they reached the capital; the emperor again ordered them to carry granted goods together with their envoys to go in reply.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven they reached the capital; the emperor again ordered them to carry gifts back with the envoys in reply.

sentences.zh: 明年，其酋遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: The next year, its chieftain dispatched envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year its chieftain again sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 撒馬兒罕酋哈裏者，哈烈酋兄子也，二人不相能，數構兵。

translations.literal: Samarkand's chieftain Khalili was the Herat chieftain's elder brother's son; the two were incompatible and repeatedly raised troops against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Khalili, chieftain of Samarkand, was the nephew of Herat's ruler; the two were at odds and repeatedly went to war.

sentences.zh: 帝因其使臣還，命都指揮白阿兒忻台齎敕諭之曰：「天生民而立之君，俾各遂其生。

translations.literal: Because their envoys were returning, the emperor ordered regional commander Bai A'ertai to carry an edict instructing them, saying: Heaven gave birth to the people and established rulers for them, causing each to fulfill his life.
translations.idiomatic: When their envoys were about to return, the emperor ordered the regional commander Bai A'ertai to carry an edict, saying: Heaven created the people and set rulers over them so that each might live in peace.

sentences.zh: 朕統禦天下，一視同仁，無間遐邇，屢嘗遣使諭爾。

translations.literal: I rule and govern all under Heaven, treating all with one kindness, without distinction between near and far; repeatedly I have sent envoys to instruct you.
translations.idiomatic: I rule all under Heaven and treat all alike, near and far without distinction, and have repeatedly sent envoys to instruct you.

sentences.zh: 爾能虔修職貢，撫輯人民，安於西徼，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: You were able devoutly to maintain tribute duties, soothe and gather the people, and be secure on the western frontier—I greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: You have dutifully maintained tribute, governed your people, and kept the western frontier at peace, and I have greatly commended this.

sentences.zh: 比聞爾與從子哈裏構兵相仇，朕為惻然。

translations.literal: Recently I heard that you and your nephew Khalili raised troops in mutual enmity; I was moved to compassion.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that you and your nephew Khalili have taken up arms against each other, and I am deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 一家之親，恩愛相厚，足制外侮。

translations.literal: Kin of one family, love and affection thick between them, are sufficient to restrain outer insult.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single family, mutual love and affection are enough to repel outside enemies.

sentences.zh: 親者尚爾乖戾，疏者安得協和。

translations.literal: If those close are still thus perverse and rebellious, how can those distant attain harmony?
translations.idiomatic: If kin turn against one another, how can strangers hope to live in harmony?

sentences.zh: 自今宜休兵息民，保全骨肉，共用太平之福。」

translations.literal: From now you should cease troops and give rest to the people, preserve flesh and bone kin, and together share the blessing of great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth you should cease hostilities, spare your people, preserve your kinship, and together enjoy the blessings of peace.

sentences.zh: 因賜彩幣表裏，並敕諭哈裏罷兵，亦賜彩幣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted colored silks inside and out, and also instructed Khalili to cease troops, likewise granting colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted colored silks, outer and inner, and also instructed Khalili to cease hostilities, granting him colored silks as well.

sentences.zh: 白阿兒忻台既奉使，遍詣撒馬兒罕、失剌思、俺的幹、俺都淮、土魯番、火州、柳城、哈實哈兒諸國，賜之幣帛，諭令入朝。

translations.literal: Bai A'ertai, having received his mission, everywhere went to Samarkand, Shiraz, Andigan, Andahuai, Turfan, Huozhou, Liucheng, Kashgar, and various states, granting them silks and cloth, instructing them to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Having received his commission, Bai A'ertai traveled to Samarkand, Shiraz, Andigan, Andahuai, Turfan, Huozhou, Liucheng, Kashgar, and other states, granting silks and instructing their rulers to come to court.

sentences.zh: 諸酋長咸喜，各遣使偕哈烈使臣貢獅子、西馬、文豹諸物。

translations.literal: All the chieftains were pleased; each dispatched envoys together with Herat's envoys to offer lions, western horses, patterned leopards, and various goods.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftains were all pleased and each sent envoys with those from Herat, offering lions, western horses, snow leopards, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 十一年達京師。

translations.literal: In year eleven they reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven they reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，禦殿受之，犒賜有加。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, held court in the hall to receive them, and consolation gifts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, received them in audience in the main hall, and granted them lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 自是諸國使並至，皆序哈烈於首。

translations.literal: From this the envoys of various states all came together, all ranking Herat first.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter envoys from many states arrived together, with Herat always given precedence.

sentences.zh: 及歸，命中官李達、吏部員外郎陳誠、戶部主事李暹、指揮金哈藍伯等送之，就齎璽書、文綺、紗羅、布帛諸物分賜其酋。

translations.literal: When they returned, the emperor ordered eunuch Li Da, Ministry of Personnel assistant department director Chen Cheng, Ministry of Revenue principal clerk Li Xian, commander Jin Halangbo, and others to escort them, carrying along a sealed edict, patterned silks, gauze, silk, cloth, and various goods to distribute and grant to their chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: When they departed, he ordered the eunuch Li Da, Chen Cheng of the Ministry of Personnel, Li Xian of the Ministry of Revenue, Commander Jin Halangbo, and others to escort them home, bearing sealed edicts, brocades, gauzes, silks, and cloth to distribute among the chieftains.

sentences.zh: 十三年，達等還，哈烈諸國復遣使偕來，貢文豹、西馬及他方物。

translations.literal: In year thirteen, Da and the others returned; Herat and various states again sent envoys together, offering patterned leopards, western horses, and goods of other regions.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen Li Da and his party returned, and Herat and other states again sent envoys together, offering snow leopards, western horses, and other regional products.

sentences.zh: 明年再貢，及還，命陳誠齎書幣報之，所過州縣皆宴餞。

translations.literal: The next year they again offered tribute; when they returned, the emperor ordered Chen Cheng to carry a letter and silks in reply; every prefecture and county they passed feasted and saw them off.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again, and when they departed the emperor ordered Chen Cheng to carry a letter and silks in reply; every prefecture and county along the route entertained them.

sentences.zh: 十五年遣使隨誠等來貢。

translations.literal: In year fifteen they dispatched envoys to follow Cheng and the others in coming to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen they sent envoys to accompany Chen Cheng and his party with tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年復貢，命李達等報如初。

translations.literal: The next year they again offered tribute; the emperor ordered Li Da and the others to reply as before.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again, and the emperor ordered Li Da and his party to respond as before.

sentences.zh: 十八年偕於闐、八答黑商來貢。

translations.literal: In year eighteen they came to offer tribute together with Khotan and Badakhshan.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen they came to court with Khotan and Badakhshan.

sentences.zh: 二十年復偕于闐來貢。

translations.literal: In year twenty they again came to offer tribute together with Khotan.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty they again came to court with Khotan.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年，其頭目打剌罕亦不剌來朝，貢馬。

translations.literal: In Xuande year two, its chieftain Darqan Ibilai came to court and offered horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande its chieftain Darqan Ibilai came to court and presented horses.

sentences.zh: 自仁宗不勤遠略，宣宗承之，久不遣使絕域，故其貢使亦稀至。

translations.literal: From Renzong not diligently pursuing distant strategy, Xuanzong inheriting this, for long not dispatching envoys to remote regions—therefore their tribute envoys also rarely arrived.
translations.idiomatic: From the Renzong emperor onward the court did not pursue distant ventures, and the Xuande emperor followed suit, so that envoys were long not sent to remote lands and tribute missions became rare.

sentences.zh: 七年復命中官李貴通西域，敕諭哈烈酋沙哈魯曰：「昔朕皇祖太宗文皇帝臨禦之日，爾等尊事朝廷，遣使貢獻，始終如一。

translations.literal: In year seven he again ordered eunuch Li Gui to open communications with the Western Regions, instructing Herat's chieftain Shahrukh, saying: Formerly when my imperial grandfather the Taizong Wendi emperor held court, you honored and served the court, dispatching envoys to offer tribute, beginning and end as one.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he again ordered the eunuch Li Gui to open communications with the Western Regions and instructed Herat's chieftain Shahrukh: In the days when my imperial grandfather, the Taizong Wendi emperor, ruled, you honored the court and sent tribute envoys without fail from first to last.

sentences.zh: 今朕恭膺天命，即皇帝位，主宰萬方，紀元宣德。

translations.literal: Now I respectfully received Heaven's mandate, immediately took the emperor's throne, ruled the ten thousand directions, and established the era name Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have reverently received Heaven's mandate, ascended the throne, rule all the realm, and have proclaimed the Xuande era.

sentences.zh: 小大政務，悉體皇祖奉天恤民，一視同仁之心。

translations.literal: Great and small government affairs all embody my imperial grandfather's heart of serving Heaven and cherishing the people, treating all with one kindness.
translations.idiomatic: In great affairs and small I embody my imperial grandfather's devotion to Heaven, his care for the people, and his equal kindness to all.

sentences.zh: 前遣使臣齎書幣往賜，道阻而回。

translations.literal: Previously I dispatched envoys bearing letters and silks to go grant gifts; the road was blocked and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys I sent earlier with letters and silks were turned back because the route was blocked.

sentences.zh: 今已開通，特命內臣往諭朕意。

translations.literal: Now it is already opened and connected; specially ordering inner court officials to go instruct my intent.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the route is open again, I have specially ordered palace officials to convey my intentions.

sentences.zh: 其益順天心，永篤誠好，相與還往，同為一家，俾商旅通行，各遂所願，不亦美乎？」

translations.literal: You should further obey Heaven's heart, forever keep sincere friendship, mutually go back and forth, become one family, causing merchants and travelers to pass, each fulfilling his wish—is this not beautiful?
translations.idiomatic: Obey Heaven's will all the more, keep your friendship sincere and lasting, exchange visits as one family, let merchants and travelers pass freely, and let each attain his desire—would that not be excellent?

sentences.zh: 因賜以文綺、羅錦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he granted patterned silks and gauze brocades.
translations.idiomatic: He then granted brocades and gauze brocades.

sentences.zh: 貴等未至，其貢使法虎兒丁已抵京師，卒於館。

translations.literal: Gui and the others had not yet arrived when their tribute envoy Faghur al-Din had already reached the capital and died in the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Before Li Gui arrived, their tribute envoy Faghur al-Din had already reached the capital and died in the guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 命官致祭，有司營葬。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered officials to perform sacrifice; the responsible offices arranged burial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered officials to perform funeral rites, and the responsible offices arranged his burial.

sentences.zh: 尋復遣使隨貴貢駝馬、玉石。

translations.literal: Soon they again dispatched envoys to follow Gui in offering camels, horses, and jade stones.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward they again sent envoys with Li Gui, presenting camels, horses, and jade.

sentences.zh: 明年春，使者歸。

translations.literal: The next spring, the envoys returned.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring the envoys returned.

sentences.zh: 復命貴護送，賜其王及頭目彩幣。

translations.literal: Again the emperor ordered Gui to escort them back and granted their king and chieftains colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again ordered Li Gui to escort them home and granted colored silks to their king and chieftains.

sentences.zh: 是年秋及正統三年並來貢。

translations.literal: That autumn and in Zhengtong year three they both came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn and again in the third year of Zhengtong they both sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十六年，甘肅巡撫楊博言：「西域入貢人多，宜為限制。」

translations.literal: In Jiajing year twenty-six, Gansu grand coordinator Yang Bo said: Western Region persons entering tribute are many; it is fitting to set limits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing, Yang Bo, grand coordinator of Gansu, said: Too many people from the Western Regions are coming on tribute missions, and limits should be imposed.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「祖宗故事，惟哈密每年一貢，貢三百人，送十一赴京，餘留關內，有司供給。

translations.literal: The ritual officials said: Ancestral precedent—only Hami once yearly offers tribute, tribute of three hundred persons, sending eleven to the capital, the rest remaining within the passes, supplied by responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual officials replied: By ancestral precedent only Hami sent tribute once a year, with a mission of three hundred men, of whom eleven were escorted to the capital while the rest remained inside the passes under official provision.

sentences.zh: 他若哈烈、哈三、土魯番、天方、撒馬兒罕諸國，道經哈密者，或三年、五年一貢，止送三五十人，其存留賞賚如哈密例。

translations.literal: As for others such as Herat, Hasan, Turfan, Mecca, Samarkand, and various states whose roads pass through Hami—some offer tribute every three or five years, sending only thirty or fifty persons; those who remain, rewards and grants follow Hami's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: As for Herat, Hasan, Turfan, Mecca, Samarkand, and other states whose routes passed through Hami, tribute came every three or five years with only thirty or fifty men escorted onward; those who remained behind were supplied and rewarded according to the Hami precedent.

sentences.zh: 頃來濫放入京，宜敕邊臣恪遵此例，濫放者罪之。」

translations.literal: Recently many have been allowed into the capital indiscriminately; frontier officials should be ordered strictly to observe this precedent, and those who allow entry indiscriminately should be punished.'
translations.idiomatic: Recently too many tributary parties had been admitted to the capital without authorization; frontier officials were ordered to enforce this rule strictly, and those who admitted entrants improperly would be punished.

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 然是時哈烈已久不至，嗣後朝貢遂絕。

translations.literal: Yet by this time Herat had long failed to come; thereafter court tribute ceased.
translations.idiomatic: By then Herat had long ceased to send missions, and tribute from that state ended altogether.

sentences.zh: 其國在西域最強大。

translations.literal: This state was the strongest in the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Herat was the most powerful state in the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 王所居城，方十餘里。

translations.literal: The city where the king dwelt was more than ten li square.
translations.idiomatic: The royal city measured more than ten li on each side.

sentences.zh: 壘石為屋，平方若高臺，不用樑柱瓦甓，中敞，虛空數十間。

translations.literal: They piled stone to make houses, square and flat like high platforms, using no beams, pillars, or tiles; the interior was open, with dozens of empty chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Houses were built of stacked stone, square and level like raised platforms, without beams, pillars, or roof tiles; the interior was open, with dozens of vacant chambers.

sentences.zh: 囪牖門扉，悉雕刻花文，繪以金碧。

translations.literal: Chimneys, windows, and doors were all carved with floral patterns and painted in gold and azure.
translations.idiomatic: Chimneys, windows, and doors were carved with floral designs and gilded in gold and azure.

sentences.zh: 地鋪氈罽，無君臣、上下、男女，相聚皆席地趺坐。

translations.literal: The floor was laid with felt and rugs; without distinction of ruler and subject, superior and inferior, or male and female, when assembled all sat cross-legged on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Floors were covered with felt and rugs; regardless of rank or sex, everyone sat cross-legged on the ground when gathered together.

sentences.zh: 國人稱其王曰鎖魯檀，猶言君長也。

translations.literal: The people called their king Sultan, meaning lord and chief.
translations.idiomatic: The people called their king Sultan, meaning simply their ruler.

sentences.zh: 男髡首纏以白布，婦女亦白布蒙首，僅露雙目。

translations.literal: Men shaved their heads and wrapped them in white cloth; women also veiled their heads in white cloth, exposing only their two eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Men shaved their heads and wrapped them in white cloth; women likewise covered their heads in white, showing only their eyes.

sentences.zh: 上下相呼皆以名。

translations.literal: Superiors and inferiors addressed one another only by personal name.
translations.idiomatic: People of every rank addressed one another by personal name alone.

sentences.zh: 相見止稍屈身，初見則屈一足三跪，男女皆然。

translations.literal: On meeting one only slightly bowed the body; on first meeting one bent one knee and knelt three times—men and women alike.
translations.idiomatic: On meeting, one bowed slightly; on a first meeting one bent one knee and knelt three times, whether man or woman.

sentences.zh: 食無匕箸，有瓷器。

translations.literal: At meals there were no spoons or chopsticks; they had porcelain vessels.
translations.idiomatic: They ate without spoons or chopsticks but used porcelain vessels.

sentences.zh: 以葡萄釀酒。

translations.literal: They made wine from grapes.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was brewed from grapes.

sentences.zh: 交易用錢，大小三等，不禁私鑄。

translations.literal: In trade they used coin, large and small in three grades; private casting was not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Commerce used coins in three sizes; private minting was permitted.

sentences.zh: 惟輸稅于酋長，用印記，無印者禁不用。

translations.literal: Only taxes were paid to the chieftain; they used seals—those without seals were forbidden and not used.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes went to the chieftain alone; transactions required his seal, and unstamped coins were rejected.

sentences.zh: 市易皆徵稅十二。

translations.literal: All market exchanges were taxed one part in twelve.
translations.idiomatic: A twelve percent tax was levied on all market trade.

sentences.zh: 不知鬥斛，止設權衡。

translations.literal: They did not know dou and hu measures; they only set up steelyards and balances.
translations.idiomatic: They did not use dry-measure standards but weighed goods on scales alone.

sentences.zh: 無官府，但有管事者，名曰刀完。

translations.literal: There were no government offices, but only administrators, called daowan.
translations.idiomatic: There were no formal government offices, only administrators called daowan.

sentences.zh: 亦無刑法，即殺人亦止罰錢。

translations.literal: There was also no penal code; even for murder the penalty was only a fine in money.
translations.idiomatic: There was no criminal law as such; even murder was punished only by a monetary fine.

sentences.zh: 以姊妹為妻妾。

translations.literal: They took sisters as wives and concubines.
translations.idiomatic: Men might marry their sisters as wives or concubines.

sentences.zh: 居喪止百日，不用棺，以布裹屍而葬。

translations.literal: Mourning lasted only one hundred days; they used no coffin but wrapped the corpse in cloth and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning lasted a hundred days; the dead were wrapped in cloth without coffins and buried.

sentences.zh: 常於墓間設祭，不祭祖宗，亦不祭鬼神，惟重拜天之禮。

translations.literal: They often set out offerings at graves; they did not sacrifice to ancestors, nor to ghosts and spirits, but only placed weight on the rite of worshipping Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: They made offerings at graves but not to ancestors or spirits, honoring above all the rite of worship toward Heaven.

sentences.zh: 無干支朔望，每七日為一轉，周而復始。

translations.literal: They had no stem-branch calendar or new and full moons; every seven days was one turn, cycling round and round.
translations.idiomatic: They kept no traditional Chinese calendar but reckoned time in seven-day cycles.

sentences.zh: 歲以二月、十月為把齋月，晝不飲食，至夜乃食，周月始茹葷。

translations.literal: Each year the second and tenth months were Ramadan months; by day they did not eat or drink, eating only at night; when the month was complete they first took meat.
translations.idiomatic: The second and tenth months were fasting months; they ate nothing by day and broke their fast at night, resuming meat only when the month ended.

sentences.zh: 城中築大土室，中置一銅器，周圍數丈，上刻文字如古鼎狀。

translations.literal: In the city they built a large earthen chamber; within they placed a bronze vessel several zhang in circumference, inscribed with characters like an ancient tripod.
translations.idiomatic: In the city stood a great earthen hall housing a bronze vessel several yards around, inscribed with characters like those on ancient tripods.

sentences.zh: 遊學者皆聚此，若中國太學然。

translations.literal: Traveling scholars all gathered here, as though it were China's Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Students from afar gathered there as at an imperial academy in China.

sentences.zh: 有善走者，日可三百里，有急使，傳箭走報。

translations.literal: There were skilled runners who could cover three hundred li in a day; for urgent dispatches they passed arrows and ran with reports.
translations.idiomatic: Fleet runners could cover three hundred li in a day; urgent messages were relayed by arrow couriers on foot.

sentences.zh: 俗尚侈靡，用度無節。

translations.literal: Custom valued extravagance; expenditures were without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved luxury and spent without restraint.

sentences.zh: 土沃饒，節候多暖少雨。

translations.literal: The soil was fertile and abundant; seasons were mostly warm with little rain.
translations.idiomatic: The land was rich and fertile, the climate mostly warm and dry.

sentences.zh: 土產白鹽、銅鐵、金銀、琉璃、珊瑚、琥珀、珠翠之屬。

translations.literal: Local products included white salt, copper, iron, gold, silver, glass, coral, amber, pearls and kingfisher feathers, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Local products included white salt, copper, iron, gold, silver, glass, coral, amber, pearls, and kingfisher feathers.

sentences.zh: 多育蠶，善為紈綺。

translations.literal: They raised many silkworms and were skilled at making fine silks.
translations.idiomatic: Silkworms were widely raised and fine silks skillfully woven.

sentences.zh: 木有桑、榆、柳、槐、松、檜，果有桃、杏、李、梨、葡萄、石榴，穀有粟、麥、麻、菽，獸有獅、豹、馬、駝、牛、羊、雞、犬。

translations.literal: Trees included mulberry, elm, willow, locust, pine, and juniper; fruits peach, apricot, plum, pear, grape, and pomegranate; grains millet, wheat, hemp, and beans; beasts lion, leopard, horse, camel, cattle, sheep, chicken, and dog.
translations.idiomatic: Trees included mulberry, elm, willow, locust, pine, and juniper; fruits included peach, apricot, plum, pear, grape, and pomegranate; grains included millet, wheat, hemp, and beans; livestock included lions, leopards, horses, camels, cattle, sheep, chickens, and dogs.

sentences.zh: 獅生於阿術河蘆林中，初生目閉，七日始開。

translations.literal: Lions were born in the reed forests along the Amu River; at birth their eyes were closed and only on the seventh day did they open.
translations.idiomatic: Lions were born in the reed marshes of the Amu River, their eyes shut until the seventh day.

sentences.zh: 土人于目閉時取之，調習其性，稍長則不可馴矣。

translations.literal: The natives took them while the eyes were still closed and trained their nature; when slightly grown they could no longer be tamed.
translations.idiomatic: Locals captured cubs while their eyes were still closed and tamed them; once grown, lions could not be domesticated.

sentences.zh: 其旁近俺都淮、八答黑商，並隸其國。

translations.literal: Andkhui and Badakhshan nearby were both subordinate to this state.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring Andkhui and Badakhshan were both subject to Herat.

sentences.zh: 俺都淮

translations.literal: Andkhui
translations.idiomatic: Andkhui

sentences.zh: 俺都淮，在哈烈西北千三百里，東南去撒馬兒罕亦如之。

translations.literal: Andkhui lay thirteen hundred li northwest of Herat; southeast to Samarkand was the same distance.
translations.idiomatic: Andkhui lay thirteen hundred li northwest of Herat and the same distance southeast of Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 城居大村，周十餘里。

translations.literal: The city stood in a large village, more than ten li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The city stood amid a large settlement, more than ten li around.

sentences.zh: 地平衍無險，田土膏腴，民物繁庶，稱樂土。

translations.literal: The land was level and open without barriers; fields were rich; people and goods abundant—it was called a land of delight.
translations.idiomatic: The land was level and unobstructed, the fields fertile, and the people prosperous—it was called a happy country.

sentences.zh: 自永樂八年至十四年偕哈烈通貢，後不復至。

translations.literal: From Yongle years eight to fourteen it sent tribute together with Herat; afterward it did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: From the eighth through the fourteenth year of Yongle it sent tribute together with Herat, but did not come again afterward.

sentences.zh: 八答黑商

translations.literal: Badakhshan
translations.idiomatic: Badakhshan

sentences.zh: 八答黑商，在俺都淮東北。

translations.literal: Badakhshan lay northeast of Andkhui.
translations.idiomatic: Badakhshan lay northeast of Andkhui.

sentences.zh: 城周十餘里。

translations.literal: The city was more than ten li in circumference.
translations.idiomatic: The city was more than ten li around.

sentences.zh: 地廣無險阻，山川明秀，人物樸茂。

translations.literal: The land was broad without barriers; mountains and rivers bright and fine; people simple and thriving.
translations.idiomatic: The country was broad and open, its mountains and rivers bright and fair, its people plain and flourishing.

sentences.zh: 浮屠數區，壯麗如王居。

translations.literal: Several Buddhist pagoda precincts were as magnificent as a king's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Several Buddhist pagoda precincts were as splendid as a royal palace.

sentences.zh: 西洋、西域諸賈多販鬻其地，故民俗富饒。

translations.literal: Western Ocean and Western Region merchants traded there extensively, so customs were prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants from the Western Ocean and the Western Regions traded there in great numbers, and the people grew wealthy.

sentences.zh: 初為哈烈酋沙哈魯之子所據。

translations.literal: At first it was held by a son of Herat's chieftain Shahrukh.
translations.idiomatic: At first it was held by a son of Shahrukh, chieftain of Herat.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年命內官把太、李達賜其酋敕書彩幣，並及哈實哈兒、葛忒郎諸部，諭以往來通商之意，皆即奉命。

translations.literal: In Yongle year six the eunuchs Ba Tai and Li Da were ordered to grant its chieftain an edict and colored silks, and also to Kashgar, Getelang, and various departments, instructing them on mutual trade; all immediately obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongle, the eunuchs Ba Tai and Li Da were sent with edicts and colored silks for its chieftain and for Kashgar, Getelang, and other departments, urging free commerce among them; all complied at once.

sentences.zh: 自是，東西萬里行旅無滯。

translations.literal: From this time, travelers east and west for ten thousand li traveled without delay.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, travelers could cross ten thousand li east and west without hindrance.

sentences.zh: 十二年，陳誠使其國。

translations.literal: In year twelve Chen Cheng was sent as envoy to their state.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve Chen Cheng was dispatched as envoy to that country.

sentences.zh: 十八年遣使來貢，命誠及內官郭敬齎書幣往報。

translations.literal: In year eighteen they sent envoys with tribute; Chen Cheng and the eunuch Guo Jing were ordered to carry letters and gifts in reply.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen they sent tribute envoys, and Chen Cheng and the eunuch Guo Jing were ordered to carry letters and gifts in return.

sentences.zh: 天順五年，其王馬哈麻遣使來貢。

translations.literal: In Tianshun year five their king Mahammad sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianshun their king Mahammad sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年復貢。

translations.literal: The next year they again sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 命使臣阿卜都剌襲父職，為指揮同知。

translations.literal: The envoy Abdula was ordered to inherit his father's post as assistant commander.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy Abdula was appointed to succeed his father as assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 于闐，古國名，自漢迄宋皆通中國。

translations.literal: Khotan, an ancient state name, from Han through Song all communicated with China.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan was an ancient state that had maintained contact with China from the Han through the Song.

sentences.zh: 永樂四年遣使來朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: In Yongle year four they sent envoys to court with local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongle they sent envoys to court with local products.

sentences.zh: 使臣辭歸，命指揮神忠母撒等齎璽書偕行，賜其酋織金文綺。

translations.literal: When the envoys took leave to return, Commander Shen Zhong Musa and others were ordered to carry a sealed edict with them and grant their chieftain brocaded silks.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys departed, Commander Shen Zhong Musa and others were sent with a sealed edict and brocaded silks for their chieftain.

sentences.zh: 其酋打魯哇亦不刺金遣使者貢玉璞，命指揮尚衡等齎書幣往勞。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Daluwa Yibulajin sent envoys with jade rough; Commander Shang Heng and others were ordered to carry letters and gifts to confer rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain Daluwa Yibulajin sent envoys with rough jade, and Commander Shang Heng and others were dispatched with letters and gifts to reward them.

sentences.zh: 十八年偕哈烈、八答黑商諸國貢馬，命參政陳誠、中官郭敬等報以彩幣。

translations.literal: In year eighteen together with Herat, Badakhshan, and other states they presented horses; Vice Commissioner Chen Cheng and the eunuch Guo Jing and others were ordered to repay with colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen they presented horses together with Herat, Badakhshan, and other states, and Vice Commissioner Chen Cheng and the eunuch Guo Jing were sent with colored silks in return.

sentences.zh: 二十年貢美玉，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: In year twenty they presented fine jade; rewards and gifts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty they presented fine jade and received especially generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 二十二年貢馬及方物。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two they presented horses and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two they presented horses and local products.

sentences.zh: 時仁宗初踐阼，即宴賚遣還。

translations.literal: At that time Renzong had just ascended the throne and immediately feasted them, granted gifts, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongxi emperor had just taken the throne; he feasted them, bestowed gifts, and sent them home at once.

sentences.zh: 先是，永樂時，成祖欲遠方萬國無不臣服，故西域之使歲歲不絕。

translations.literal: Previously, during Yongle, Chengzu desired that the myriad states of distant regions all submit; thus Western Region envoys year after year never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Yongle reign, the Yongle emperor wished every distant state to submit, and Western Region envoys came year after year without pause.

sentences.zh: 諸蕃貪中國財帛，且利市易，絡繹道途。

translations.literal: Various fan states coveted China's silks and wealth, and moreover profited from trade, crowding the roads.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier states coveted Chinese silks and goods and profited from trade, so the roads were thronged with travelers.

sentences.zh: 商人率偽稱貢使，多攜馬、駝、玉石，聲言進獻。

translations.literal: Merchants mostly falsely called themselves tribute envoys, mostly carrying horses, camels, and jade, proclaiming they came to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants commonly posed as tribute envoys, bringing horses, camels, and jade while claiming to present gifts.

sentences.zh: 既入關，則一切舟車水陸、晨昏飲饌之費，悉取之有司。

translations.literal: Once they entered the passes, then all expenses for boats, carts, land and water routes, morning and evening food and drink were all taken from the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside the frontier passes, every cost of transport by land or water and every meal was charged to the local authorities.

sentences.zh: 郵傳困供億，軍民疲轉輸。

translations.literal: Postal stations were strained supplying provisions; military and civilians were exhausted by transport.
translations.idiomatic: Postal stations buckled under the burden of supply, and soldiers and civilians were worn out by transport duties.

sentences.zh: 比西歸，輒緣道遲留，多市貨物。

translations.literal: When about to return west, they always delayed along the road, buying many goods.
translations.idiomatic: On their return westward they lingered along the route, buying goods in large quantities.

sentences.zh: 東西數千里間，騷然繁費，公私上下罔不怨咨。

translations.literal: Between east and west for several thousand li, there was uproar and heavy expense; public and private, above and below, none did not complain.
translations.idiomatic: For thousands of li east and west the roads seethed with expense, and everyone from officials to commoners complained.

sentences.zh: 廷臣莫為言，天子亦莫之恤也。

translations.literal: Court ministers did not speak on it; the Son of Heaven also did not regard it with concern.
translations.idiomatic: No court minister spoke up, and the emperor paid the matter no heed.

sentences.zh: 至是，給事中黃驥極陳其害。

translations.literal: At this time, supervising secretary Huang Ji extremely stated its harms.
translations.idiomatic: Then Supervising Secretary Huang Ji laid out the harm in the strongest terms.

sentences.zh: 仁宗感其言，召禮官呂震責讓之。

translations.literal: Renzong was moved by his words and summoned ritual official Lü Zhen to rebuke and blame him.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by his argument, the Hongxi emperor summoned the ritual official Lü Zhen and rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 自是不復使西域，貢使亦漸稀。

translations.literal: From this they no longer sent to the Western Regions; tribute envoys also gradually grew few.
translations.idiomatic: From then on missions to the Western Regions ceased, and tribute envoys grew increasingly rare.

sentences.zh: 于闐自古為大國，隋、唐間侵並戎盧、捍彌、渠勒、皮山諸國，其地益大。

translations.literal: Khotan from antiquity was a great state; between Sui and Tang it annexed Ronglu, Hanmi, Quile, Pishan, and various states, and its territory grew greater.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan had long been a great power; in the Sui and Tang it annexed Ronglu, Hanmi, Quile, Pishan, and other states, and its territory grew still larger.

sentences.zh: 南距蔥嶺二百餘里，東北去嘉峪關六千三百里。

translations.literal: South it was two hundred-odd li from the Pamirs; northeast six thousand three hundred li from Jiayu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: It lay two hundred-odd li south of the Pamirs and six thousand three hundred li northeast of Jiayu Pass.

sentences.zh: 大略蔥嶺以南，撒馬兒罕最大；

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, south of the Pamirs Samarkand was largest;
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, south of the Pamirs Samarkand was the greatest power;

sentences.zh: 以北，于闐最大。

translations.literal: north of them, Khotan was largest.
translations.idiomatic: north of the Pamirs, Khotan was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 元末時，其主暗弱，鄰國交侵。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuan, its ruler was dim and weak; neighboring states attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan its rulers were feeble, and neighboring states raided one another.

sentences.zh: 人民僅萬計，悉避居山谷，生理蕭條。

translations.literal: The population amounted to only ten thousand-odd; all fled to dwell in valleys; livelihood was desolate and sparse.
translations.idiomatic: The population fell to only ten thousand or so, all hiding in the valleys while livelihood withered.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，西域憚天子威靈，咸修職貢，不敢擅相攻，於闐始獲休息。

translations.literal: In Yongle, the Western Regions feared the Son of Heaven's august might, all maintained duty and tribute, did not dare attack one another at will; Khotan then obtained rest.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle the Western Regions feared the emperor's majesty, all sent tribute, and dared not attack one another freely; Khotan at last found peace.

sentences.zh: 漸行賈諸蕃，復致富庶。

translations.literal: Gradually merchants traveled among the various fan states; again they grew rich and prosperous.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants gradually returned among the frontier states, and prosperity was restored.

sentences.zh: 桑麻黍禾，宛然中土。

translations.literal: Mulberry, hemp, millet, and grain were just like the central provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Mulberry, hemp, millet, and grain flourished as in the central provinces.

sentences.zh: 其國東有白玉河，西有綠玉河，又西有黑玉河，源皆出昆侖山。

translations.literal: East of their state was the White Jade River, west the Green Jade River, and further west the Black Jade River; all sources issued from Kunlun Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: East of the country lay the White Jade River, to the west the Green Jade River, and farther west the Black Jade River, all rising in the Kunlun Mountains.

sentences.zh: 土人夜視月光盛處，入水采之，必得美玉。

translations.literal: The natives by night watched where moonlight was bright, entered the water to gather there, and certainly obtained fine jade.
translations.idiomatic: By night the people watched where moonlight shone brightest on the water, dove in to gather jade there, and always found fine stones.

sentences.zh: 其鄰國亦多竊取來獻。

translations.literal: Neighboring states also often secretly stole and came to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Neighboring states often seized jade illicitly and presented it as tribute.

sentences.zh: 迄萬曆朝，于闐亦間入貢。

translations.literal: Down to the Wanli reign, Khotan also occasionally entered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the Wanli reign Khotan still sent tribute from time to time.

sentences.zh: 失刺思

translations.literal: Shiraz
translations.idiomatic: Shiraz

sentences.zh: 失刺思，近撒馬兒罕。

translations.literal: Shiraz was near Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Shiraz lay near Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 永樂十一年遣使偕哈烈、俺的幹、哈實哈兒等八國，隨白阿兒忻台入貢方物，命李達、陳誠等齎敕偕其使往勞。

translations.literal: In Yongle year eleven they sent envoys together with Herat, Andigan, Kashgar, and eight states, following Bai A'erxintai to enter tribute with local products; Li Da, Chen Cheng, and others were ordered to carry edicts with their envoys to confer rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Yongle they sent envoys with Herat, Andigan, Kashgar, and seven other states, following Bai A'erxintai to present tribute; Li Da and Chen Cheng were ordered to carry edicts and escort the envoys home with rewards.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，其酋亦不剌金遣使隨達等朝貢，天子方北巡。

translations.literal: In year thirteen winter, their chieftain Yibulajin sent envoys following Da and others to court with tribute; the Son of Heaven was then on northern tour.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year thirteen their chieftain Yibulajin sent envoys with Li Da's party to present tribute while the emperor was on a northern tour.

sentences.zh: 至明年夏始辭還，復命誠偕中官魯安齎敕及白金、彩緞、紗羅、布帛賜其酋。

translations.literal: Not until the next year summer did they take leave to return; again Chen Cheng with the eunuch Lu An were ordered to carry an edict and white silver, colored damask, gauze, silk, and cloth to grant their chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: They did not take leave until the following summer, when Chen Cheng and the eunuch Lu An were again sent with an edict and gifts of silver, colored damask, gauze, silk, and cloth for their chieftain.

sentences.zh: 十七年遣使偕亦思弗罕諸部貢獅子、文豹、名馬，辭還。

translations.literal: In year seventeen they sent envoys together with Isfahan and various departments with lions, patterned leopards, and famous horses; they took leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen they sent envoys with Isfahan and other departments, presenting lions, leopards, and fine horses, then departed.

sentences.zh: 復命安等送之，賜其酋絨錦、文綺、紗羅、玉系腰、磁器諸物。

translations.literal: Again Lu An and others were ordered to escort them, granting their chieftain pile silks, patterned silks, gauze silk, jade belt ornaments, porcelain, and various things.
translations.idiomatic: Lu An and others were again ordered to escort them home and grant their chieftain pile silks, brocades, gauze, jade belt ornaments, porcelain, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 時車駕頻歲北征，乏馬，遣官多齎彩幣、磁器，市之失剌思及撒馬兒罕諸國。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage year after year campaigned north and lacked horses; officials were often dispatched carrying colored silks and porcelain to buy them in Shiraz and Samarkand and various states.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor campaigned north year after year and needed horses; officials were repeatedly sent with colored silks and porcelain to buy them in Shiraz, Samarkand, and other states.

sentences.zh: 其酋即遣使貢馬，以二十一年八月謁帝于宣府之行宮。

translations.literal: Their chieftain then sent envoys presenting horses; in year twenty-one eighth month they attended the emperor at the traveling palace at Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain then sent envoys with horses, who in the eighth month of year twenty-one met the emperor at the traveling palace in Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 厚賜之，遣還京師，其人遂久留內地不去。

translations.literal: He richly granted them and sent them back to the capital; those persons then long remained in the interior and did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded them generously and sent them on to the capital, but they lingered long in the interior and would not leave.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嗣位，趣之還，乃辭去。

translations.literal: When Renzong succeeded the throne, he urged them to return, and then they took leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongxi emperor succeeded to the throne, he urged them to return home, and at last they departed.

sentences.zh: 宣德二年貢駝馬方物，授其使臣阿力為都指揮僉事，賜誥命、冠帶。

translations.literal: In Xuande year two they presented camels, horses, and local products; their envoy Ali was appointed assistant chief commander and granted a patent of appointment and official cap and sash.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xuande they presented camels, horses, and local products; their envoy Ali was appointed assistant chief commander and granted a patent of appointment with cap and sash.

sentences.zh: 嗣後久不貢。

translations.literal: Thereafter for long they did not send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: After that they sent no tribute for a long time.

sentences.zh: 成化十九年與黑婁、撒馬兒罕、把丹沙諸國共貢獅子，詔加優賚。

translations.literal: In Chenghua year nineteen, together with Heilou, Samarkand, Badansha, and various states they jointly presented lions; an edict granted extra generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Chenghua, together with Heilou, Samarkand, Badansha, and other states, they jointly presented lions, and the court ordered especially generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，哈密忠順王陝巴襲封歸國，與鄰境野乜克力酋結婚。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year five, Hami's Loyal and Obedient Prince Sham Ba succeeded to the fief and returned to his state, marrying the chieftain of neighboring Yemekli.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi, Sham Ba of Hami, Loyal and Obedient Prince, inherited his title and returned home to marry the chieftain of neighboring Yemekli.

sentences.zh: 失剌思酋念其貧，偕旁國亦不剌因之酋，率其平章鎖和卜台、知院滿可，各遣人請頒賜財物，助之成婚。

translations.literal: Shiraz's chieftain, mindful of his poverty, together with the chieftain of neighboring Yibulajin, leading his chief minister Suohobotai and commissioner Manko, each dispatched men requesting grants of goods to assist the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The chieftain of Shiraz, pitying Sham Ba's poverty, joined with the chieftain of neighboring Yibulajin and, with his chief minister Suohobotai and commissioner Manko, each sent envoys asking the court to grant goods to help pay for the wedding.

sentences.zh: 朝議義之，厚賜陝巴，並賜二國及其平章、知院彩幣。

translations.literal: Court discussion deemed it righteous; they richly granted Sham Ba, and also granted the two states and their chief minister and commissioner colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed this was fitting, rewarded Sham Ba generously, and granted colored silks to both states and to their chief minister and commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年與旁近三十二部並遣使貢馬及方物。

translations.literal: Jiajing year three, together with thirty-two neighboring departments they all dispatched envoys presenting horses and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing, Shiraz together with thirty-two neighboring departments sent envoys presenting horses and local products.

sentences.zh: 其使者各乞蟒衣、膝襴、磁器、布帛。

translations.literal: Their envoys each begged python-pattern robes, knee-length gowns, porcelain, and cloth silks.
translations.idiomatic: Each envoy asked for python-pattern robes, knee-length gowns, porcelain, and silks.

sentences.zh: 天子不能卻，量予之，自是貢使亦不至。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven could not refuse, and measured grants were given; from this tribute envoys also did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not refuse them outright and granted gifts in moderation, but thereafter no tribute envoys came again.

sentences.zh: 俺的幹

translations.literal: Andigan
translations.idiomatic: Andigan

sentences.zh: 俺的幹，西域小部落。

translations.literal: Andigan is a small tribe of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Andigan was a small community of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 元太祖盡平西域，封子弟為王鎮之，其小者則設官置戍，同於內地。

translations.literal: The Yuan founding emperor entirely pacified the Western Regions, enfeoffing sons and younger brothers as kings to guard them; the smaller ones then had officials set and garrisons placed, the same as the interior.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan founder pacified the Western Regions, he enfeoffed kinsmen as territorial kings; smaller domains received officials and garrisons on the same model as the interior provinces.

sentences.zh: 元亡，各自割據，不相統屬。

translations.literal: When the Yuan perished, each seized territory independently, not subject to one another.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuan fell, each domain seized its own ground and acknowledged no common overlord.

sentences.zh: 洪武、永樂間，數遣人招諭，稍稍來貢。

translations.literal: Between Hongwu and Yongle, they repeatedly sent men to summon and instruct; gradually they came to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Hongwu and Yongle reigns the Ming repeatedly sent envoys to summon them, and little by little they began sending tribute.

sentences.zh: 地大者稱國，小者止稱地面。

translations.literal: Those large in territory called themselves states; the small ones only called themselves territories.
translations.idiomatic: The larger domains styled themselves states; the smaller ones called themselves mere territories.

sentences.zh: 迄宣德朝，效臣職、奉表箋、稽首闕下者，多至七八十部。

translations.literal: Down to the Xuande reign, those fulfilling ministerial duties, offering memorials and petitions, and kowtowing below the palace gate reached as many as seventy or eighty departments.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xuande reign as many as seventy or eighty polities were performing ministerial duties, submitting memorials, and kowtowing at court.

sentences.zh: 而俺的幹，則永樂十一年與哈烈並貢者也。

translations.literal: As for Andigan, it was in Yongle year eleven that it presented tribute together with Herat.
translations.idiomatic: Andigan was among those that presented tribute with Herat in the eleventh year of Yongle.

sentences.zh: 迨十四年，魯安等使哈烈、失剌思諸思，復便道賜其酋長文綺。

translations.literal: Reaching year fourteen, Lu An and others were envoys to Herat, Shiraz, and various states, again by the way granting their chieftains patterned silks.
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen the eunuch Lu An and others, while on a mission to Herat, Shiraz, and other states, again granted patterned silks to their chieftains along the route.

sentences.zh: 然地小不能常貢，後竟不至。

translations.literal: Yet the territory was small and could not offer tribute constantly; in the end they did not come.
translations.idiomatic: But the domain was too small to tribute regularly, and in time its envoys stopped coming altogether.

sentences.zh: 哈實哈兒

translations.literal: Kashgar
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar

sentences.zh: 哈實哈兒，亦西域小部落。

translations.literal: Kashgar is also a small tribe of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar was likewise a small community of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年，把太、李達等齎敕往賜，即奉命。

translations.literal: Yongle year six, Ba Tai, Li Da, and others carried an edict to go grant gifts; they immediately obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongle, Ba Tai and Li Da carried an imperial edict with gifts, and its ruler obeyed at once.

sentences.zh: 十一年遣使隨白阿兒忻台入朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: Year eleven they dispatched envoys following Bai A'erxintai to enter court, presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven they sent envoys with Bai A'erxintai to court, presenting local products.

sentences.zh: 宣德時亦來朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Xuande era they also came to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xuande reign they also came to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 天順七年命指揮劉福、普賢使其地。

translations.literal: Tianshun year seven ordered commanders Liu Fu and Puxian to mission to their territory.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianshun the court sent commanders Liu Fu and Puxian as envoys to their territory.

sentences.zh: 其貢使亦不能常至。

translations.literal: Their tribute envoys also could not come constantly.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute envoys likewise could not come on a regular schedule.

sentences.zh: 亦思弗罕

translations.literal: Isfahan
translations.idiomatic: Isfahan

sentences.zh: 亦思弗罕，地近俺的幹。

translations.literal: Isfahan's territory is near Andigan.
translations.idiomatic: Isfahan lay near Andigan.

sentences.zh: 永樂十四年使俺都淮、撒馬兒罕者道經其地，賜其酋文綺諸物。

translations.literal: Yongle year fourteen those on mission to Andahuai and Samarkand passed through its territory and granted its chieftain patterned silks and various goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yongle envoys bound for Andahuai and Samarkand passed through Isfahan and granted its chieftain patterned silks and other goods.

sentences.zh: 十七年偕鄰國失剌思共貢獅、豹、西馬，賚白金、鈔幣。

translations.literal: Year seventeen together with neighboring state Shiraz they jointly presented lions, leopards, and western horses; white silver and paper money were bestowed in return.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen, together with neighboring Shiraz, they presented lions, leopards, and western horses and received grants of silver and paper money in return.

sentences.zh: 使臣辭還，命魯安等送之。

translations.literal: The envoys took leave to return; Lu An and others were ordered to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys took their leave, Lu An and others were ordered to escort them home.

sentences.zh: 有馬哈木者，願留京師。

translations.literal: There was one Mahammad who wished to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: One envoy named Mahammad asked to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 從其請。

translations.literal: His request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 成化十九年與撒馬兒罕共貢獅子、名馬、番刀、兜羅、鎖幅諸物，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: Chenghua year nineteen together with Samarkand they jointly presented lions, famous horses, foreign knives, gauze, and brocade silks and various things; grants and gifts were increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Chenghua, together with Samarkand, they presented lions, fine horses, foreign knives, gauze, and brocades, and received especially generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 先是，宣德六年，有亦思把罕遣使臣迷兒阿力朝貢，或云即亦思弗罕。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Xuande year six, there was Isbahhan dispatching the envoy Mir Ali to court with tribute; some say this was Isfahan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the sixth year of Xuande, a place called Isbahhan sent the envoy Mir Ali to court; some identify it with Isfahan.

sentences.zh: 火剌劄

translations.literal: Hulazha
translations.idiomatic: Hulazha

sentences.zh: 火剌劄，國微弱。

translations.literal: Hulazha—the state was feeble and small.
translations.idiomatic: Hulazha was a feeble little state.

sentences.zh: 四圍皆山，鮮草木。

translations.literal: On all four sides are mountains; plants and trees are few.
translations.idiomatic: Mountains surrounded it on every side, and vegetation was sparse.

sentences.zh: 水流曲折，亦無魚蝦。

translations.literal: Streams winding and twisting, yet there are no fish or shrimp.
translations.idiomatic: Its streams wound tortuously, yet held no fish or shrimp.

sentences.zh: 城僅里許，悉土屋，酋所居亦卑陋。

translations.literal: The city is barely a li across; all are earthen houses, and even where the chieftain dwells is low and shabby.
translations.idiomatic: The city measured barely a li across; all dwellings were of earth, and even the chieftain's residence was mean and cramped.

sentences.zh: 俗敬僧。

translations.literal: The custom honors monks.
translations.idiomatic: The people held monks in reverence.

sentences.zh: 永樂十四年遣使朝貢，命所經地皆禮待。

translations.literal: Yongle year fourteen they dispatched envoys to court with tribute; they were ordered to receive courteous treatment in every place they passed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yongle its envoys came to court, and every place along their route was ordered to receive them courteously.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年，其地回回怕魯灣等由海道貢玻璃、瑪瑙諸物。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year five, Muslims Parvan and others from its territory by sea route presented glass, agate, and various things.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi, Muslims from the region including Parvan came by sea, presenting glass, agate, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 孝宗不納，賜道里費遣還。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong did not accept them; he granted traveling expenses and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: The Hongzhi emperor declined the tribute, granted travel expenses, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 乞力麻兒

translations.literal: Kilimar
translations.idiomatic: Kilimar

sentences.zh: 乞力麻兒，永樂中遣使來貢，惟獸皮、鳥羽、罽褐。

translations.literal: Kilimar—in the Yongle era dispatched envoys to present tribute, only animal hides, bird feathers, and felt rugs.
translations.idiomatic: Kilimar sent envoys during the Yongle reign, offering only animal hides, bird feathers, and felt rugs.

sentences.zh: 其俗喜射獵，不事耕農。

translations.literal: Their custom delights in shooting and hunting; they do not engage in plowing and farming.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved hunting and did not practice agriculture.

sentences.zh: 西南傍海，東北林莽深密，多猛獸、毒蟲。

translations.literal: Southwest it borders the sea; northeast forest and thicket are deep and dense, with many fierce beasts and poisonous insects.
translations.idiomatic: To the southwest it bordered the sea; to the northeast lay dense forest teeming with fierce beasts and venomous creatures.

sentences.zh: 有逵巷，無市肆，交易用鐵錢。

translations.literal: There are broad lanes but no market stalls; trade uses iron money.
translations.idiomatic: It had broad lanes but no marketplaces, and trade was conducted in iron coin.

sentences.zh: 白松虎兒

translations.literal: Baisonghu'er
translations.idiomatic: Baisonghu'er

sentences.zh: 白松虎兒，舊名速麻裏兒。

translations.literal: Baisonghu'er—its former name was Sumalai'er.
translations.idiomatic: Baisonghu'er had formerly been called Sumalai'er.

sentences.zh: 嘗有白虎出松林中，不傷人，亦不食他獸，旬日後不復見。

translations.literal: Once a white tiger emerged from the pine forest, harming no person and also eating no other beast; after ten days it was seen no more.
translations.idiomatic: Once a white tiger appeared from the pine forest; it harmed no one, preyed on no other animal, and after ten days was seen no more.

sentences.zh: 國人異之，稱為神虎，曰此西方白虎所降精也，因改國名。

translations.literal: The people of the state marveled at it, calling it a divine tiger, saying this was the essence descended from the western White Tiger, and so changed the state name.
translations.idiomatic: The people were astonished and called it a divine tiger, saying it was the spirit of the western White Tiger descended to earth, and renamed the state accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其地無大山，亦不生樹木，無毒蟲、猛獸之害，然物產甚薄。

translations.literal: Its territory has no great mountains, also does not produce trees; there is no harm from poisonous insects or fierce beasts, yet products of the land are very scant.
translations.idiomatic: The land had no great mountains and produced no timber; poisonous creatures and fierce beasts did not trouble it, yet its resources were very meager.

sentences.zh: 永樂中嘗入貢。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era they once entered with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign it sent tribute once.

sentences.zh: 答兒密

translations.literal: Darim
translations.idiomatic: Darim

sentences.zh: 答兒密，服屬撒馬兒罕。

translations.literal: Darim is subject to Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Darim was subject to Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 居海中，地不百里，人不滿千家。

translations.literal: It dwells amid the sea; the territory is not a hundred li, the people not a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: It stood in the sea; its territory did not reach a hundred li and its population numbered fewer than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 無城郭，上下皆居板屋。

translations.literal: There are no walls or cities; above and below all dwell in plank houses.
translations.idiomatic: It had no walled towns; everyone lived in plank houses raised above the water.

sentences.zh: 知耕植，有毛褐、布縷、馬駝、牛羊。

translations.literal: They know plowing and planting; they have felt rugs, cloth strands, horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: They practiced farming and kept felt cloth, woven goods, horses, camels, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 刑止箠樸。

translations.literal: Punishment stops at flogging and cudgels.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment went no further than flogging and clubbing.

sentences.zh: 交易兼用銀錢。

translations.literal: In trade they also use silver money.
translations.idiomatic: Trade was conducted in both silver and cash coin.

sentences.zh: 永樂中遣使朝貢，賜《大統曆》及文綺、藥、茶諸物。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era they dispatched envoys to court with tribute; they were granted the Great Unity Calendar and patterned silks, medicines, tea, and various things.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle its envoys came to court and received the Great Unity Calendar, brocades, medicines, tea, and other gifts.

sentences.zh: 納失者罕

translations.literal: Nasireh
translations.idiomatic: Nasireh

sentences.zh: 納失者罕，東去失剌思數日程，皆舟行。

translations.literal: Nasireh is several days' journey east of Shiraz; all travel is by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Nasireh lay several days' journey east of Shiraz, entirely reachable by boat.

sentences.zh: 城東平原，饒水草，宜畜牧。

translations.literal: East of the city is level plain, rich in water and grass, suitable for livestock raising.
translations.idiomatic: East of the city stretched level plain rich in pasture, well suited to herding.

sentences.zh: 馬有數種，最小者高不過三尺。

translations.literal: Horses have several kinds; the smallest are no more than three chi in height.
translations.idiomatic: Its horses came in several breeds; the smallest stood no more than three feet high.

sentences.zh: 俗重僧，所至必供飲食。

translations.literal: The custom esteems monks; wherever they arrive they must be supplied food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: The people held monks in high regard and always offered them food and drink wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 然好氣健鬥，鬥不勝者，眾嗤之。

translations.literal: Yet they love spirit and are strong in fighting; those who do not win in combat are all ridiculed by the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they were quarrelsome and fond of fighting; anyone who lost in a brawl was mocked by the crowd.

sentences.zh: 永樂中遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era they dispatched envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle they sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 使臣還，曆河北，轉關中，抵甘肅，有司皆置宴。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned, they passed through Hebei, turned to Guanzhong, reached Gansu; every office set feasts.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the envoys traveled through Hebei, turned west through Guanzhong to Gansu, and officials in every locality entertained them at feast.

sentences.zh: 敏真城，永樂中來貢。

translations.literal: Minzhencheng—in the Yongle era came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Minzhencheng sent tribute during the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 其國地廣，多高山。

translations.literal: Its state's territory is broad, with many high mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory was broad and mountainous.

sentences.zh: 日中為市，諸貨駢集，貴中國磁、漆器。

translations.literal: At midday they make the market; all goods gather in throngs; they prize Chinese porcelain and lacquerware.
translations.idiomatic: Markets opened at midday with goods crowded in profusion; Chinese porcelain and lacquerware were especially prized.

sentences.zh: 產異香、駝、馬。

translations.literal: They produce exotic incense, camels, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: It produced rare incense, camels, and horses.

sentences.zh: 米昔兒

translations.literal: Misr
translations.idiomatic: Misr

sentences.zh: 米昔兒，一名密思兒。

translations.literal: Misr—one name is Misir.
translations.idiomatic: Misr, also called Misir—Egypt.

sentences.zh: 永樂中遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the Yongle era they dispatched envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongle they sent envoys to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 既宴賚，命五日一給酒饌、果餌，所經地皆置宴。

translations.literal: After feast and grants, they were ordered given wine fare and fruit delicacies once every five days; every place they passed set feasts.
translations.idiomatic: After the court feast and gifts, they were supplied wine and fruit every five days, and officials along the route held banquets for them.

sentences.zh: 正統六年，王鎖魯檀阿失剌福復來貢。

translations.literal: Zhengtong year six, the king Sultan Ashraf again came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhengtong the king Sultan Ashraf came again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「其地極遠，未有賜例。

translations.literal: The ritual official said: 'Its territory is extremely remote; there is no precedent for grants.
translations.idiomatic: The director of rites reported: 'Its territory is extremely remote, and there is no precedent for gifts.

sentences.zh: 昔撒馬兒罕初貢時，賜予過優，今宜稍損。

translations.literal: Formerly when Samarkand first offered tribute, gifts were excessively generous; now it is fitting to reduce somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: When Samarkand first sent tribute the court was overly generous; the grant should now be somewhat reduced.

sentences.zh: 賜王彩幣十表裏，紗、羅各三匹，白氁絲布、白將樂布各五匹，洗白布二十匹，王妻及使臣遞減。」

translations.literal: Grant the king ten sets of colored silks inside and out, three bolts each of gauze and silk gauze, five bolts each of white felted silk cloth and white Jiangle cloth, twenty bolts of washed white cloth; the king's wife and envoys receive reduced amounts in order.
translations.idiomatic: Grant the king ten sets of colored silks, three bolts each of gauze and gauze silk, five bolts each of white felted silk and white Jiangle cloth, and twenty bolts of bleached white cloth, with lesser amounts for the queen and envoys in descending order.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 自後不復至。

translations.literal: From then on they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: After that they did not come again.

sentences.zh: 黑婁，近撒馬兒罕，世為婚姻。

translations.literal: Heilou is near Samarkand; generation after generation they have been united by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Heilou lay near Samarkand and had been linked by marriage for generations.

sentences.zh: 其地山川、草木、禽獸皆黑，男女亦然。

translations.literal: Its territory's mountains, rivers, plants, trees, birds, and beasts are all black; men and women are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Its mountains and rivers, plants and animals were all black, and so were its men and women.

sentences.zh: 宣德七年遣使來朝，貢方物。

translations.literal: Xuande year seven they dispatched envoys to come to court, presenting local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xuande they sent envoys to court with local products.

sentences.zh: 正統二年，其王沙哈魯鎖魯檀遣指揮哈只馬黑麻奉貢。

translations.literal: Zhengtong year two, its king Shahrukh Sultan dispatched the commander Hajji Mahammad to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengtong its king Shahrukh Sultan sent the commander Hajji Mahammad with tribute.

sentences.zh: 命齎敕及金織糸寧絲、彩絹歸賜其王。

translations.literal: They were ordered to carry an edict and gold-woven ramie silk and colored silks home to grant their king.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to carry home an imperial edict and gifts of gold-woven ramie silk and colored silks for their king.

sentences.zh: 六年復來貢。

translations.literal: Year six they again came with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year six they came again with tribute.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年偕鄰境三十一部男婦百余人，貢馬二百四十有七，騾十二，驢十，駝七，及玉石、碸砂、鑌鐵刀諸物。

translations.literal: Jingtai year four, together with thirty-one neighboring departments, more than a hundred men and women presented two hundred forty-seven horses, twelve mules, ten donkeys, seven camels, and jade, realgar, wrought-iron knives, and various things.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jingtai, together with thirty-one neighboring departments, more than a hundred men and women presented two hundred forty-seven horses, twelve mules, ten donkeys, seven camels, jade, realgar, wrought-iron knives, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 天順七年，王母塞亦遣指揮僉事馬黑麻舍兒班等奉貢。

translations.literal: Tianshun year seven, the queen mother Saiyi dispatched the assistant regional commander Mahammad Shahban and others to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianshun the queen mother Saiyi sent the assistant regional commander Mahammad Shahban and others with tribute.

sentences.zh: 賜彩幣表裏、糸寧、絲襲衣，擢其使臣為指揮同知，從者七人俱為所鎮撫。

translations.literal: They were granted colored silks inside and out, ramie silk, and silk ceremonial robes; their envoy was promoted to vice commander, and seven followers all became garrison commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: They received colored silks, ramie, and silk ceremonial robes; the envoy was promoted to vice commander, and seven followers were all appointed garrison commissioners.

sentences.zh: 成化十九年與失剌思、撒馬兒罕、把丹沙共貢獅子。

translations.literal: Chenghua year nineteen together with Shiraz, Samarkand, and Badansha they jointly presented lions.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Chenghua, together with Shiraz, Samarkand, and Badansha, they jointly presented lions.

sentences.zh: 把丹沙之長亦稱鎖魯檀馬黑麻，景泰七年嘗入貢，至是復偕至。

translations.literal: Badansha's chief also styled himself Sultan Mahammad; in Jingtai year seven he had once entered with tribute, and on this occasion came again together with them.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of Badansha also styled himself Sultan Mahammad; he had sent tribute in the seventh year of Jingtai and now came again with them.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年又與天方諸國貢駝、馬、玉石。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year three again together with Mecca and various states they presented camels, horses, and jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongzhi they again presented camels, horses, and jade together with Mecca and other states.

sentences.zh: 討來思

translations.literal: Tolays
translations.idiomatic: Tolays

sentences.zh: 討來思，地小，周徑不百里。

translations.literal: Tolays—the territory is small, its circumference not a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Tolays was a small domain less than a hundred li in circumference.

sentences.zh: 城近山。

translations.literal: The city is near the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Its city stood close to the mountains.

sentences.zh: 山下有水，赤色，望之如火。

translations.literal: Below the mountains is water, red in color; viewed from afar it seems like fire.
translations.idiomatic: Below the mountains ran water of red hue that, seen from afar, looked like fire.

sentences.zh: 俗佞佛。

translations.literal: The custom is devoted to Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: The people were fervently devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 婦人主家柄。

translations.literal: Women hold the household authority.
translations.idiomatic: In Tollis, women held authority within the household.

sentences.zh: 產牛羊馬駝，有布縷毛褐。

translations.literal: It produces cattle, sheep, horses, and camels; there are cloth, thread, and woolen felts.
translations.idiomatic: Tollis produced cattle, sheep, horses, and camels, and cloth, yarn, and woolen felts.

sentences.zh: 土宜穄麥，無稻。

translations.literal: The soil suits panic millet and wheat; there is no rice.
translations.idiomatic: The soil favored panic millet and wheat; rice did not grow there.

sentences.zh: 交易用錢。

translations.literal: In trade they use money.
translations.idiomatic: Commerce was conducted with coin.

sentences.zh: 宣德六年入貢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuande they entered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Xuande reign Tollis sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 明年命中官李貴齎璽書獎勞，賜文綺、彩帛。

translations.literal: The next year the court ordered the eunuch Li Gui to bear an imperial seal letter of reward and consolation, granting patterned silks and colored silks.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the court sent the eunuch Li Gui with an imperial letter of commendation and consolation, granting figured silks and colored silks.

sentences.zh: 以地小不能常貢。

translations.literal: Because the territory was small they could not regularly present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Because Tollis was too small to sustain regular missions, tribute could not be sent often.

sentences.zh: 阿速，近天方、撒馬兒罕，幅員甚廣。

translations.literal: Asud lies near Mecca and Samarkand; its territory is very broad.
translations.idiomatic: Asud lay near Mecca and Samarkand and covered a very broad territory.

sentences.zh: 城倚山面川。

translations.literal: The city leans on mountains and faces a river valley.
translations.idiomatic: Its capital stood against the mountains and opened onto a river valley.

sentences.zh: 川南流入海，有魚鹽之利。

translations.literal: A river to the south flows into the sea; there is profit in fish and salt.
translations.idiomatic: A river to the south ran to the sea, yielding fish and salt.

sentences.zh: 土宜耕牧。

translations.literal: The soil suits farming and pasturing.
translations.idiomatic: The land was fit for both farming and grazing.

sentences.zh: 敬佛畏神，好施惡鬥。

translations.literal: They revere the Buddha and fear the spirits; they love giving alms and hate fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The people revered the Buddha, feared the divine, loved charity, and shunned strife.

sentences.zh: 物產富，寒暄適節，人無饑寒，夜鮮寇盜，雅稱樂土。

translations.literal: Products are abundant; cold and heat suit the seasons; people know neither hunger nor cold; at night bandits are few—the land is commonly called a happy realm.
translations.idiomatic: Goods were plentiful, the seasons mild, and the people free of hunger and cold; bandits were rare by night, and the country was famed as a land of ease.

sentences.zh: 永樂十七年，其酋牙忽沙遣使貢馬及方物，宴賚如制。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yongle its chieftain Yahshah dispatched envoys to present horses and local products; banquets and rewards followed the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Yongle its chieftain Yahshah sent envoys with horses and local products; banquets and rewards followed the usual regulations.

sentences.zh: 以地遠不能常貢。

translations.literal: Because the land was distant they could not regularly present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Its distance made regular tribute impossible.

sentences.zh: 天順七年命都指揮白全等使其國，竟不復再貢。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianshun the court ordered Regional Commander Bai Quan and others to envoy to their state; ultimately they never again presented tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Tianshun the court sent Regional Commander Bai Quan and others as envoys to their state, but thereafter they never sent tribute again.

sentences.zh: 沙哈魯

translations.literal: Sharhrud
translations.idiomatic: Sharhrud

sentences.zh: 沙哈魯，在阿速西海島中。

translations.literal: Sharhrud lies on an island in the western sea near Asud.
translations.idiomatic: Sharhrud lay on an island in the western sea off Asud.

sentences.zh: 永樂中遣七十七人來貢，日給酒饌、果餌，異於他國。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign they sent seventy-seven persons to present tribute; daily they were supplied wine, food, and fruit confections—differing from other states.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign seventy-seven tribute bearers came; each day they were given wine, meals, and fruit confections—a treatment unlike that for other states.

sentences.zh: 其地，山川環抱，饒畜產，人性樸直，恥鬥好佛。

translations.literal: Its lands are embraced by mountains and rivers; livestock products are abundant; the people's nature is simple and straight; they are ashamed to fight and fond of Buddhism.
