translations.idiomatic: Mountains and rivers enclosed the land, livestock was plentiful, and the people were plain and upright, ashamed of fighting and devoted to Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 王及臣僚處城中，庶人悉處城處。

translations.literal: The king and his ministers dwell within the city; all commoners dwell outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: The king and his officials lived inside the city; commoners all lived outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 海產奇物，西域賈人以輕直市之，其國人不能識。

translations.literal: Strange things come from the sea; Western Region merchants buy them at low prices; the people of the state cannot identify them.
translations.idiomatic: Strange things came from the sea; Western merchants bought them cheaply, while the islanders themselves could not name them.

sentences.zh: 天方，古筠沖地，一名天堂，又曰默伽。

translations.literal: Mecca—anciently the land of Junchong; one name is Paradise; it is also called Mecca.
translations.idiomatic: Mecca was anciently the land of Junchong, also called Paradise and known as Mecca.

sentences.zh: 不道自忽魯謨斯四十日始至，自古裏西南行，三月始至。

translations.literal: From Hormuz by the overland route it is forty days; from Calicut traveling southwest it is three months.
translations.idiomatic: By sea from Hormuz the voyage takes forty days; from Calicut, traveling southwest, three months.

sentences.zh: 其貢使多從陸道入嘉峪關。

translations.literal: Their tribute envoys mostly enter by the land route through Jiayu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Most of its tribute envoys came overland through Jiayu Pass.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，鄭和使西洋，分遣其儕詣古裏。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande Zheng He was missioned to the Western Ocean and separately sent his colleagues to Calicut.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xuande, Zheng He sailed to the Western Ocean and sent some of his companions on to Calicut.

sentences.zh: 聞古裏遣人往天方，因使人齎貨物附其舟偕行。

translations.literal: Hearing that Calicut was sending people to Mecca, he therefore had men carry goods to attach to their ship and travel together.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Calicut was dispatching a party to Mecca, he sent men with goods to join their ship.

sentences.zh: 往返經歲，市奇珍異寶及麒麟、獅子、駝雞以歸。

translations.literal: Going and returning took a year; they purchased rare treasures and curiosities, and giraffes, lions, and ostriches to return.
translations.idiomatic: The round trip took a year; they bought rare treasures, giraffes, lions, and ostriches and brought them back.

sentences.zh: 其國王亦遣陪臣隨朝使來貢。

translations.literal: That state's king also sent attendant ministers to follow the court envoys and come to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The king also sent attendant ministers to follow the imperial envoys and present tribute.

sentences.zh: 宣宗喜，賜賚有加。

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor was pleased and added to their rewards and grants.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande Emperor was pleased and increased their rewards.

sentences.zh: 正統元年始命附爪哇貢舟還，賜幣及敕獎其王。

translations.literal: From the first year of Zhengtong they were first ordered to return attached to Java's tribute ship; coins and an imperial edict were granted to reward its king.
translations.idiomatic: From the first year of Zhengtong they were sent home on Java's tribute fleet, and the court granted silks and an edict commending their king.

sentences.zh: 六年，王遣子賽亦得阿力與使臣賽亦得哈三以珍寶來貢。

translations.literal: In year six the king sent his son Sayyid Ali and the envoy Sayyid Hasan with precious treasures to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the king sent his son Sayyid Ali and the envoy Sayyid Hasan with precious goods as tribute.

sentences.zh: 陸行至哈剌，遇賊，殺使臣，傷其子右手，盡劫貢物以去，命守臣察治之。

translations.literal: Traveling by land they reached Khara; they met bandits who killed the envoys, wounded the son's right hand, and completely looted the tribute goods and left; the court ordered border officials to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: On the overland route they reached Khara, where bandits killed the envoys, wounded the prince's right hand, and seized all the tribute before fleeing; the court ordered local officials to investigate.

sentences.zh: 成化二十三年，其國中回回阿力以兄納的游中土四十餘載，欲往雲南訪求。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua, a Muslim in their state named Ali, because his elder brother Nadi had wandered in China for more than forty years, wished to go to Yunnan to search for him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year of Chenghua a Muslim of that country named Ali, whose elder brother Nadi had lived in China for more than forty years, wished to go to Yunnan to find him.

sentences.zh: 乃攜寶物钜萬，至滿剌加，附行人左輔舟，將入京進貢。

translations.literal: He therefore carried treasure worth tens of thousands, reached Melaka, and attached to the traveler Zuo Fu's ship, intending to enter the capital and present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: He took goods worth a fortune to Melaka, joined the traveler Zuo Fu's ship, and planned to enter the capital and offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 抵廣東，為市舶中官韋眷侵克。

translations.literal: On reaching Guangdong, the maritime trade superintendent eunuch Wei Juan extorted and seized from him.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangdong the maritime-trade eunuch Wei Juan cheated and squeezed him.

sentences.zh: 阿力怨，赴京自訴。

translations.literal: Ali resented this and went to the capital to plead his own case.
translations.idiomatic: Ali, furious, went to the capital to plead his case in person.

sentences.zh: 禮官請估其貢物，酬其直，許訪兄于雲南。

translations.literal: The rites officials requested to appraise his tribute goods and compensate their value, permitting him to search for his brother in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites proposed appraising his goods, paying their value, and allowing him to search for his brother in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時眷懼罪，先已夤緣於內。

translations.literal: At that time Juan feared punishment and had already made secret connections within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: By then Juan, fearing punishment, had already secured patrons inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝乃責阿力為間諜，假貢行奸，令廣東守臣逐還，阿力乃號泣而去。

translations.literal: The emperor then accused Ali of being a spy who used tribute as a pretext to commit treachery, ordered Guangdong border officials to expel and return him, and Ali departed wailing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor declared Ali a spy who had used tribute as cover for intrigue, ordered Guangdong officials to send him back, and Ali left in tears.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年，其王速檀阿黑麻遣使偕撒馬兒罕、土魯番貢馬、駝、玉石。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi its king Sultan Ahmad dispatched envoys together with Samarkand and Turfan to present horses, camels, and jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongzhi its king Sultan Ahmad sent envoys with Samarkand and Turfan bearing horses, camels, and jade.

sentences.zh: 正德初，帝從禦馬太監谷大用言，令甘肅守臣訪求諸番騍馬、騸馬，番使雲善馬出天方。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, following Grand Eunuch of the Imperial Stud Gu Dayong, the emperor ordered Gansu border officials to seek out fine stallions and geldings from the various fan states; fan envoys said fine horses came from Mecca.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde, at the urging of the imperial stud eunuch Gu Dayong, the emperor told Gansu officials to seek fine stallions and geldings from the western states; envoys said the best horses came from Mecca.

sentences.zh: 守臣因請諭諸番貢使，傳達其王，俾以入貢。

translations.literal: Border officials therefore requested that tribute envoys from the various fan be instructed to convey to their kings that they should enter tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials therefore asked that tribute envoys be told to urge their kings to send horses.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書劉宇希中官指，議令守臣善擇使者與通事，親詣諸番曉諭，從之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liu Yu favored the eunuch's intent; it was proposed that border officials carefully choose envoys and interpreters to go in person to instruct the various fan—this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Liu Yu sided with the eunuch and proposed that border officials choose reliable envoys and interpreters to go in person and instruct the western states; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，王寫亦把剌克遣使貢馬、駝、梭幅、珊瑚、寶石、魚牙刀諸物，詔賜蟒龍金織衣及麝香、金銀器。

translations.literal: In year thirteen King Shah Bakr dispatched envoys to present horses, camels, saffron fabrics, coral, gems, fish-tooth knives, and various objects; an edict granted python-dragon gold-woven robes and musk and gold and silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen King Shah Bakr sent horses, camels, saffron cloth, coral, gems, and fish-tooth knives; the court granted python-dragon brocade robes, musk, and gold and silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年，其王亦麻都兒等遣使貢馬、駝、方物。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing its king Imad al-Din and others dispatched envoys to present horses, camels, and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiajing its king Imad al-Din and others sent horses, camels, and local products.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「西人來貢，陝西行都司稽留半年以上始為具奏。

translations.literal: Rites officials said: "When westerners come to present tribute, the Shaanxi Branch Regional Military Commission detains them for more than half a year before reporting.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites said: "When westerners arrive on tribute, the Shaanxi regional command holds them for more than half a year before reporting.

sentences.zh: 所進玉石悉粗惡，而使臣所私貨皆良。

translations.literal: The jade they present is all coarse and inferior, while what the envoys privately trade are all fine.
translations.idiomatic: The jade presented as tribute is coarse, while what the envoys trade privately is fine.

sentences.zh: 乞下按臣廉問，自今毋得多攜玉石，煩擾道途。

translations.literal: We beg that investigating censors be sent to inquire impartially; from now on they must not carry too much jade and trouble the roads.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that censors investigate, and that hereafter they be forbidden to carry excessive jade and burden the roads.

sentences.zh: 其貢物不堪者，治都司官罪。」

translations.literal: For tribute goods that are not acceptable, punish the officials of the regional command.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute goods are unworthy, the regional command officials should be punished.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 明年，其國額麻都抗等八王各遣使貢玉石，主客郎中陳九川簡退其粗惡者，使臣怨。

translations.literal: The next year eight kings of that state including Imad al-Ghan each dispatched envoys to present jade; Supervisor of Receptions Chen Jiuchuan culled and rejected the coarse and inferior; the envoys were resentful.
translations.idiomatic: The next year eight kings including Imad al-Ghan each sent jade; Chen Jiuchuan of the Receptions Office rejected the poor pieces, and the envoys were angry.

sentences.zh: 通事胡士紳亦憾九川因詐為使臣奏，詞誣九川，盜玉，坐下詔獄拷訊。

translations.literal: Interpreter Hu Shishen also bore a grudge against Jiuchuan and therefore falsely submitted a petition in the envoys' name, with words impeaching Jiuchuan for stealing jade; he was imprisoned and interrogated under imperial order.
translations.idiomatic: Interpreter Hu Shishen, who also hated Jiuchuan, forged a petition in the envoys' name accusing him of stealing jade; Jiuchuan was thrown into prison and interrogated.

sentences.zh: 尚書席書、給事中解一貫等論救，不聽，竟戍邊。

translations.literal: Minister Xi Shu, supervising secretary Xie Yiguan, and others argued for mercy; the emperor would not listen and in the end banished Jiuchuan to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xi Shu and supervising secretary Xie Yiguan pleaded for him, but the emperor refused and banished Jiuchuan to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 十一年遣使偕土魯番、撒馬兒罕、惟密諸國來貢，稱王者至三十七人。

translations.literal: In year eleven they dispatched envoys together with Turfan, Samarkand, Weimi, and various states to present tribute; those calling themselves kings reached thirty-seven persons.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven envoys came with Turfan, Samarkand, Weimi, and other states; thirty-seven men styled themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 禮官言：「舊制，恰哈密與朵顏三衛比歲一貢，貢不過三百人。

translations.literal: Rites officials said: "Former regulations provided that Hami and the Ordos Three Guards each presented tribute once a year, with tribute envoys not exceeding three hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites said: "By old rule Hami and the Ordos Three Guards each sent tribute once a year, with no more than three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 三衛地近，盡許入都。

translations.literal: The Three Guards are near; all may be permitted to enter the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Three Guards were near, all might enter the capital.

sentences.zh: 哈密則十遣其二，余留待于邊。

translations.literal: For Hami, only two of every ten envoys; the rest are kept waiting at the border.
translations.idiomatic: For Hami only two in ten were sent on; the rest waited at the border.

sentences.zh: 若西域則越在萬里，素非屬國，難視三衛貢期，而所遣使人倍逾恒數。

translations.literal: As for the Western Regions, they lie ten thousand li away and have never been subordinate states; it is hard to treat their tribute schedule like the Three Guards', yet the envoys they send exceed the usual number twofold.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Regions lie ten thousand li away and were never subject states; their schedule cannot be treated like the Three Guards', yet they now send more than twice the usual number.

sentences.zh: 番文至二百餘通，皆以索取叛人牙木蘭為詞。

translations.literal: Fan documents reached more than two hundred, all using the demand for the rebel Yaliban as their pretext.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred western memorials arrived, all demanding the rebel Yaliban.

sentences.zh: 竊恐托詞窺伺，以覘朝廷處分。

translations.literal: We fear this is a pretext to spy and observe how the court will dispose of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: We fear this is a pretext to spy on how the court will respond.

sentences.zh: 邊臣不遵明例，概行起送，有乖法體。

translations.literal: Border officials do not follow the clear precedents and send them all on indiscriminately—this violates statutory form.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials ignore precedent and forward everyone, contrary to law.

sentences.zh: 乞下督撫諸臣，遇諸番人入貢，分別存留起送，不得概遣入京。

translations.literal: We beg that supervising and pacifying officials be ordered: when various fan persons enter tribute, distinguish whom to keep and whom to send on; they must not be indiscriminately dispatched to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that governors and pacifiers be ordered, when western peoples come on tribute, to decide who stays and who goes on, and not send all to the capital.

sentences.zh: 且嚴飭邊吏，毋避禍目前，貽患異日，貪納款之虛名，忘禦邊之實策。」

translations.literal: And strictly admonish border officials not to avoid present trouble and bequeath calamity for another day, greedily accepting empty praise for submission while forgetting real policy for frontier defense.
translations.idiomatic: And warn border officials not to court present peace and future disaster, grasping at empty credit for submission while forgetting real frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 帝可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved their memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 故事，諸番貢物至，邊臣驗上其籍，禮官為按籍給賜。

translations.literal: By precedent, when various fan tribute goods arrived, border officials inspected and forwarded their registers; rites officials distributed rewards according to the registers.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when tribute goods arrived, border officials checked the register and the Ministry of Rites gave rewards according to it.

sentences.zh: 籍所不載，許自行貿易。

translations.literal: What the registers did not list was permitted for private trade.
translations.idiomatic: Goods not on the register might be traded privately.

sentences.zh: 貢使既竣，即有餘貨，責令攜歸。

translations.literal: Once tribute envoys had finished, if there remained surplus goods, they were ordered to carry them back.
translations.idiomatic: After the tribute mission ended, any surplus had to be taken home.

sentences.zh: 願入官者，禮官奏聞，給鈔。

translations.literal: Those who wished to surrender to the state: rites officials memorialized and paper money was given.
translations.idiomatic: If they wished to sell to the state, the Ministry of Rites memorialized and paid in paper money.

sentences.zh: 正德末，黠番猾胥交關罔利，始有貿易余貨令市儈評直、官給絹鈔之例。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengde, crafty fan and cunning clerks engaged in collusion for illicit profit; there began the precedent of trade in surplus goods whereby brokers appraised value and officials gave silk and paper money.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhengde, crafty westerners and corrupt clerks colluded for profit, and a precedent arose for surplus goods to be appraised by brokers and paid for in silk and notes.

sentences.zh: 至是，天方及土魯番使臣，其籍余玉石、銼刀諸貨，固求准貢物給賞。

translations.literal: At this time Mecca and Turfan envoys had jade, knives, and other goods left on their registers beyond tribute; they firmly requested rewards on the same terms as tribute goods.
translations.idiomatic: Now Mecca and Turfan envoys had jade, knives, and other goods left on the register and insisted on receiving tribute rewards for them.

sentences.zh: 禮官不得已，以正德間例為請，許之。

translations.literal: Rites officials had no choice and requested using the Zhengde precedent; this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites, having no choice, cited the Zhengde precedent and the court allowed it.

sentences.zh: 番使多賈人，來輒挾重貲與中國市。

translations.literal: Fan envoys are mostly merchants; when they come they always carry heavy assets to trade with China.
translations.idiomatic: Western envoys were mostly merchants who arrived laden with goods to trade in China.

sentences.zh: 邊吏嗜賄，侵克多端，類取償於公家。

translations.literal: Border officials are greedy for bribes and practice many forms of extortion and seizure, generally taking repayment from the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials took bribes and extorted in many ways, often making the state pay.

sentences.zh: 或不當其直，則咆哮不止。

translations.literal: Or when the price did not suit them, they would roar and not stop.
translations.idiomatic: If the price did not suit them, they would storm and rage without end.

sentences.zh: 是歲，貢使皆黠悍，既習知中國情，且憾邊吏之侵克也，屢訴之，禮官卻不問。

translations.literal: That year the tribute envoys were all crafty and fierce; having learned China's circumstances and bearing resentment at border officials' extortion, they complained repeatedly, but rites officials paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: That year the envoys were sharp and fierce; knowing China's ways and angry at border extortion, they complained again and again, but the Ministry of Rites ignored them.

sentences.zh: 鎮守甘肅中官陳浩者，當番使入貢時，令家奴王洪多索名馬、玉石諸物，使臣憾之。

translations.literal: Chen Hao, the eunuch defending Gansu, when fan envoys entered tribute had his household slave Wang Hong demand many famous horses, jade, and other things—the envoys resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hao, the eunuch commanding Gansu, had his servant Wang Hong demand famous horses, jade, and other goods when envoys came; they resented it.

sentences.zh: 一日，遇洪於衢，即執詣官以證實其事。

translations.literal: One day encountering Hong in the street, they immediately seized him and brought him before officials to verify the matter.
translations.idiomatic: One day they seized Hong in the street and dragged him before officials to prove the case.

sentences.zh: 禮官言事關國體，須大有處分，以服遠人之心。

translations.literal: Rites officials said the affair concerned national dignity and required severe disposition to satisfy distant peoples' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites said the matter touched national dignity and required stern punishment to satisfy distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 乃命三法司、錦衣衛及給事中各遣官一員赴甘肅按治，洪迄獲罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Three Offices of Justice, the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and supervising secretaries each dispatched one official to Gansu to investigate; Hong in the end was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Judicial Offices, the Embroidered Uniform Guard, and the supervising secretaries each sent an official to Gansu to investigate; Hong was punished in the end.

sentences.zh: 十七年復貢，其使臣請遊覽中土。

translations.literal: In year seventeen they again presented tribute; their envoys requested to tour the central land.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen they sent tribute again; their envoys asked to tour the interior.

sentences.zh: 禮官疑有狡心，以非故事格之。

translations.literal: Rites officials suspected crafty intent and refused on grounds it was not precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Rites suspected intrigue and refused, saying it was not precedent.

sentences.zh: 二十二年偕撒馬兒罕、土魯番、哈密、魯迷諸國貢馬及方物。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two together with Samarkand, Turfan, Hami, Rum, and various states they presented horses and local products.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two they came with Samarkand, Turfan, Hami, Rum, and other states bearing horses and local products.

sentences.zh: 後五六年一貢，迄萬曆中不絕。

translations.literal: Thereafter tribute came once every five or six years, continuing without break through the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter tribute came every five or six years without fail through the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 天方於西域為大國，四時常似夏，無雨雹霜雪，惟露最濃，草木皆資之長養。

translations.literal: Mecca is a great state among the Western Regions; the four seasons are constantly like summer; there is no rain, hail, frost, or snow—only dew is thickest; grass and trees all rely on it for growth.
translations.idiomatic: Mecca was the greatest state of the Western Regions; all four seasons felt like summer, without rain, hail, frost, or snow—only heavy dew on which plants depended.

sentences.zh: 土沃，饒栗、麥、黑黍。

translations.literal: The soil is fertile; millet, wheat, and black millet are abundant.
translations.idiomatic: The soil was rich in millet, wheat, and black millet.

sentences.zh: 人皆頎碩。

translations.literal: The people are all tall and well built.
translations.idiomatic: The people were tall and sturdy.

sentences.zh: 男子削髮，以布纏之。

translations.literal: Men shave their hair and wrap it with cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Men shaved their heads and bound them with cloth.

sentences.zh: 婦女則編發蓋頭，不露其面。

translations.literal: Women braid their hair and cover their heads, not exposing their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Women braided their hair and veiled their faces.

sentences.zh: 相傳回回設教之祖曰馬哈麻者，首於此地行教，死即葬焉。

translations.literal: It is handed down that the ancestor of the Muslims who established the teaching, called Muhammad, first practiced the teaching in this place; when he died he was buried there.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that Muhammad, founder of the Muslim faith, first preached here and was buried here when he died.

sentences.zh: 墓頂常有光，日夜不熄。

translations.literal: Over the tomb there is constantly light, day and night unextinguished.
translations.idiomatic: A light shone over the tomb day and night without ceasing.

sentences.zh: 後人遵其教，久而不衰，故人皆向善。

translations.literal: Later people followed his teaching, long without decline; therefore the people all incline toward goodness.
translations.idiomatic: His followers kept the faith unbroken, and the people were inclined to goodness.

sentences.zh: 國無苛擾，亦無刑罰，上下安和，寇賊不作，西土稱為樂國。

translations.literal: The state has no harsh exactions, nor any punishments; above and below are peaceful and harmonious; bandits do not arise—the western lands call it a happy realm.
translations.idiomatic: There were no harsh levies and little punishment; high and low lived in peace, bandits were unknown, and the west called it a land of joy.

sentences.zh: 俗禁酒。

translations.literal: Custom forbids wine.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was forbidden by custom.

sentences.zh: 有禮拜寺，月初生，其王及臣民鹹拜天，號呼稱揚以為禮。

translations.literal: There are mosques; at the new moon the king and subjects all worship heaven, crying out and proclaiming as ritual.
translations.idiomatic: There were mosques; at the new moon king and people worshipped heaven with cries and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 寺分四方，每方九十間，共三百六十間，皆白玉為柱，黃甘玉為地。

translations.literal: The mosque is divided into four quarters; each quarter ninety rooms, altogether three hundred sixty rooms—all with white jade pillars and yellow sweet jade flooring.
translations.idiomatic: The mosque had four wings of ninety bays each, three hundred sixty in all, with white jade pillars and yellow jade floors.

sentences.zh: 其堂以五色石砌成，四方平頂。

translations.literal: Its hall is built of five-colored stone, with a flat roof on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The main hall was built of five-colored stone with a flat roof.

sentences.zh: 內用沉香大木為梁凡五，又以黃金為閣。

translations.literal: Within, fragrant eaglewood beams number five in all; also a pavilion of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Inside were five great beams of eaglewood and a golden pavilion.

sentences.zh: 堂中垣墉，悉以薔薇露、龍涎香和土為之。

translations.literal: The hall's walls and ramparts are all made of earth mixed with rose dew and ambergris.
translations.idiomatic: The walls were of earth mixed with rosewater and ambergris.

sentences.zh: 守門以二黑獅。

translations.literal: Two black lions guard the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Two black lions guarded the gate.

sentences.zh: 堂左有司馬儀墓，其國稱為聖人塚。

translations.literal: To the left of the hall is the tomb of Simayi; their state calls it the Tomb of the Sage.
translations.idiomatic: To the left of the hall stood a tomb the country called the Sage's Mound.

sentences.zh: 土悉寶石，圍牆則黃甘玉。

translations.literal: The ground is all precious stones; the enclosing walls are yellow sweet jade.
translations.idiomatic: The ground was paved with precious stone, the enclosing walls with yellow jade.

sentences.zh: 兩旁有諸祖師傳法之堂，亦以石築成，俱極其壯麗。

translations.literal: On both sides are halls where various patriarchs transmitted the teaching, also built of stone, all extremely magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: On either side stood halls where patriarchs had transmitted the faith, likewise built of stone and magnificently grand.

sentences.zh: 其崇奉回回教如此。

translations.literal: Their reverence for the Muslim teaching is like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was their devotion to the Muslim faith.

sentences.zh: 瓜果、諸畜，鹹如中國。

translations.literal: Fruits, melons, and various livestock are all like China.
translations.idiomatic: Fruits, melons, and livestock were much like those of China.

sentences.zh: 西瓜、甘瓜有一人不能舉者，桃有重四五斤者，雞、鴨有重十餘斤者，皆諸番所無也。

translations.literal: Watermelons and sweet melons include some one man cannot lift; peaches weigh four or five jin; chickens and ducks weigh more than ten jin—all things the various foreign lands lack.
translations.idiomatic: Some watermelons and sweet melons were too heavy for one man to lift; peaches weighed four or five pounds, chickens and ducks more than ten—produce unknown among other foreign lands.

sentences.zh: 馬哈麻墓後有一井，水清而甘。

translations.literal: Behind Muhammad's tomb there is a well; its water is clear and sweet.
translations.idiomatic: Behind Muhammad's tomb was a well of clear, sweet water.

sentences.zh: 泛海者必汲以行，遇颶風，取水灑之即息。

translations.literal: Those who sail the sea must draw from it for the voyage; encountering a hurricane, sprinkling the water stops it.
translations.idiomatic: Seafarers always drew from it before sailing; if a hurricane struck, sprinkling the water was said to calm the storm.

sentences.zh: 當鄭和使西洋時，傳其風物如此。

translations.literal: When Zheng He was envoy to the Western Ocean, its products and scenery were reported thus.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng He sailed to the Western Ocean, such were the reports of its sights and products.

sentences.zh: 其後稱王者至二三十人，其俗亦漸不如初矣。

translations.literal: Afterward those styling themselves kings reached twenty or thirty persons, and its customs gradually were no longer as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Later as many as twenty or thirty men styled themselves kings, and local customs slowly declined from what they had been.

sentences.zh: 默德那

translations.literal: Medina
translations.idiomatic: Medina

sentences.zh: 默德那，回回祖國也，地近天方。

translations.literal: Medina is the ancestral land of the Muslims; its territory lies near Mecca.
translations.idiomatic: Medina was the ancestral homeland of the Muslims, near Mecca.

sentences.zh: 宣德時，其酋長遣使偕天方使臣來貢，後不復至。

translations.literal: In the Xuande era its chieftain sent envoys together with Mecca's envoys to offer tribute; afterward they did not come again.
translations.idiomatic: During Xuande its chief sent envoys with those from Mecca to court, but they did not return thereafter.

sentences.zh: 相傳，其初國王謨罕驀德生而神靈，盡臣服西域諸國，諸國尊為別諳拔爾，猶言天使也。

translations.literal: It is handed down that the first king Muhammad was born with divine power, made all states of the Western Regions submit, and the states honored him as Bi'anba'er, meaning an angel.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that the first king Muhammad was born with miraculous power, brought the Western Regions to submission, and was honored as Bi'anba'er—meaning an angel.

sentences.zh: 國中有經三十本，凡三千六百余段。

translations.literal: Within the state there are thirty scriptures, altogether more than three thousand six hundred sections.
translations.idiomatic: The country possessed thirty scriptures in more than three thousand six hundred sections.

sentences.zh: 其書旁行，兼篆、草、楷三體，西洋諸國皆用之。

translations.literal: Its books are written in columns across the page, combining seal, cursive, and regular scripts; all states of the Western Ocean use them.
translations.idiomatic: Their script ran horizontally and combined seal, cursive, and regular forms; states of the Western Ocean all used it.

sentences.zh: 其教以事天為主，而無像設。

translations.literal: Its teaching takes serving Heaven as primary, and has no images or fixtures.
translations.idiomatic: The faith centered on worship of Heaven and used no images.

sentences.zh: 每日西向虔拜。

translations.literal: Every day they devoutly worship facing west.
translations.idiomatic: Each day they prayed devoutly facing west.

sentences.zh: 每歲齋戒一月，沐浴更衣，居必易常處。

translations.literal: Each year they fast one month, bathe and change clothes, and when dwelling must change their usual place.
translations.idiomatic: Each year they fasted for a month, bathing and changing clothes and moving to a different dwelling.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，其國撒哈八撒阿的幹葛思始傳其教入中國。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, their country's Sa'ad ibn Abi Waqqas first transmitted its teaching into China.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaihuang era of Sui, Sa'ad ibn Abi Waqqas of that land first brought the faith to China.

sentences.zh: 迄元世，其人遍于四方，皆守教不替。

translations.literal: By the Yuan age their people were spread throughout the four quarters, all keeping the teaching without decline.
translations.idiomatic: By Yuan times their people were scattered everywhere, yet all kept the faith unbroken.

sentences.zh: 國中城池、宮室、市肆、田園，大類中土。

translations.literal: Within the state, walled cities, palaces, markets, and fields and gardens largely resemble the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: Its walled towns, palaces, markets, and farmland resembled those of the central provinces.

sentences.zh: 有陰陽、星曆、醫藥、音樂諸技。

translations.literal: They have the arts of yin-yang, astronomy and calendrics, medicine, and music.
translations.idiomatic: They practiced yin-yang lore, astronomy, medicine, and music.

sentences.zh: 其織文、制器尤巧。

translations.literal: Their woven patterns and crafted vessels are especially ingenious.
translations.idiomatic: Their weaving and metalwork were especially fine.

sentences.zh: 寒暑應候，民殷物繁，五穀六畜鹹備。

translations.literal: Cold and heat follow the seasons; the people are prosperous and goods abundant; the five grains and six livestock are all complete.
translations.idiomatic: Seasons turned in their course; the people were prosperous and goods plentiful, with grain and livestock in full supply.

sentences.zh: 俗重殺，不食豬肉。

translations.literal: Custom esteems slaughter; they do not eat pork.
translations.idiomatic: They valued ritual slaughter and did not eat pork.

sentences.zh: 嘗以白布蒙頭，雖適他邦，亦不易其俗。

translations.literal: They always cover their heads with white cloth; even when they go to other states, they do not change this custom.
translations.idiomatic: They wrapped their heads in white cloth and kept the custom even abroad.

sentences.zh: 坤城，西域回回種。

translations.literal: Kuncheng is a Muslim people of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Kuncheng was a Muslim community of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年，其使臣者馬力丁等來朝，貢駝馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xuande its envoy Mali Ding and others came to court, presenting camels and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xuande its envoy Mali Ding and others came to court with camels and horses.

sentences.zh: 時有開中之令，使者即輸米一萬六千七百石於京倉中鹽。

translations.literal: At the time there was an order for opening the middle exchange; the envoys at once delivered sixteen thousand seven hundred shi of grain to the capital granaries for salt.
translations.idiomatic: Under the open-exchange policy then in force, the envoys at once delivered sixteen thousand seven hundred shi of grain to the capital granaries in exchange for salt.

sentences.zh: 及辭還，願以所納米獻官。

translations.literal: When taking leave to return, they wished to present the grain they had delivered to the authorities.
translations.idiomatic: On departing they offered to present the grain they had paid to the government.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「回人善營利，雖名朝貢，實圖貿易，可酬以直。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Muslims are skilled at profit; though called court tribute, in truth they seek trade—compensate them with fair value.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Muslims are skilled at profit; though this is called tribute, they truly seek trade—pay them fair value.

sentences.zh: 於是予帛四十匹、布倍之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were given forty bolts of silk and twice as much cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They were therefore given forty bolts of silk and twice as much cloth.

sentences.zh: 其後亦嘗貢。

translations.literal: Afterward they also sometimes offered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: They sent tribute on later occasions as well.

sentences.zh: 自成祖以武定天下，欲威制萬方，遣使四出招徠。

translations.literal: From the time the Chengzu emperor settled the realm by arms, wishing to awe and control the ten thousand regions, he sent envoys in all directions to summon and win over.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongle emperor conquered the realm by force, he sought to awe every quarter and sent envoys abroad to win allegiance.

sentences.zh: 由是西域大小諸國莫不稽顙稱臣，獻琛恐後。

translations.literal: Hence the great and small states of the Western Regions all bowed their foreheads and styled themselves subjects, fearing to be late in presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon great and small states of the Western Regions bowed in submission and rushed to offer tribute.

sentences.zh: 又北窮沙漠，南極溟海，東西抵日出沒之處，凡舟車可至者，無所不屆。

translations.literal: Again north to the end of the desert, south to the utmost sea, east and west reaching where the sun rises and sets—wherever boat or cart could reach, nothing was not attained.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys ranged north to the desert's edge, south to the open sea, and east and west to the limits of sunrise and sunset; wherever ship or cart could go, they arrived.

sentences.zh: 自是，殊方異域鳥言侏亻離之使，輻輳闕廷。

translations.literal: From this, envoys of strange lands and foreign realms with bird speech and dwarf tongues converged like wheel spokes at the court.
translations.idiomatic: From then on envoys from distant lands with strange speech crowded the palace.

sentences.zh: 歲時頒賜，庫藏為虛。

translations.literal: Seasonal grants and gifts emptied the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal gifts drained the treasuries bare.

sentences.zh: 而四方奇珍異寶、名禽殊獸進獻上方者，亦日增月益。

translations.literal: Yet rare treasures and strange goods, famous birds and exotic beasts presented to the throne also increased day by day and month by month.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rare treasures, exotic birds, and strange beasts presented to the throne grew ever more numerous.

sentences.zh: 蓋兼漢、唐之盛而有之，百王所莫並也。

translations.literal: Thus combining the splendor of Han and Tang and possessing both, no hundred kings could be compared.
translations.idiomatic: The court combined the glory of Han and Tang in one age—unmatched by any earlier reign.

sentences.zh: 餘威及於後嗣，宣德、正統朝猶多重譯而至。

translations.literal: Surplus awe reached later descendants; in the Xuande and Zhengtong reigns many still came through multiple interpreters.
translations.idiomatic: Its prestige lingered into later reigns; during Xuande and Zhengtong many envoys still arrived through layers of interpreters.

sentences.zh: 然仁宗不務遠略，踐阼之初，即撤西洋取寶之船，停松花江造舟之役，召西域使臣還京，敕之歸國，不欲疲中土以奉遠人。

translations.literal: Yet the Renzong emperor did not pursue distant strategies; at the beginning of his accession he at once withdrew the Western Ocean treasure ships, halted shipbuilding on the Songhua River, summoned Western Region envoys back to the capital, and ordered them to return home, unwilling to weary the central lands to serve distant people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Renzong sought no distant ambitions; at the start of his reign he recalled the Western Ocean treasure fleet, halted shipbuilding on the Songhua, summoned Western envoys to the capital and sent them home, unwilling to exhaust the empire for distant guests.

sentences.zh: 宣德繼之，雖間一遣使，尋亦停止，以故邊隅獲休息焉。

translations.literal: Xuande succeeded him; though occasionally sending envoys once, soon he also stopped, and for this reason the border regions obtained rest.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande followed his example; though he occasionally sent envoys, he soon stopped as well, and the frontier thus found respite.

sentences.zh: 哈三等二十九部

translations.literal: Hasan and twenty-nine other divisions
translations.idiomatic: Hasan and Twenty-nine Other Districts

sentences.zh: 今采故牘嘗奉貢通名天朝者，曰哈三，曰哈烈兒，曰沙的蠻，曰哈的蘭，曰掃蘭，曰乜克力，曰把力黑，曰俺力麻，曰脫忽麻，曰察力失，曰幹失，曰卜哈剌，曰怕剌，曰你沙兀兒，曰克失迷兒，曰帖必力思，曰火壇，曰火占，曰苦先，曰牙昔，曰牙兒幹，曰戎，曰白，曰兀倫，曰阿端，曰邪思城，曰舍黑，曰擺音，曰克，計二十九部。

translations.literal: Now selecting from old documents those that once offered tribute and communicated their names to the Celestial Court: called Hasan, called Harar, called Shadianman, called Hadilan, called Saolan, called Yikeli, called Balihei, called Anlima, called Tuohuma, called Chalishi, called Ganshi, called Buhala, called Pala, called Nishawuer, called Kashmir, called Tiebili, called Huotan, called Huozhan, called Kuxian, called Yaxi, called Yargan, called Rong, called Bai, called Wulun, called Aduan, called Yesicheng, called Shehei, called Baiyin, called Kefu—in all twenty-nine divisions.
translations.idiomatic: From old records we list those that once sent tribute and registered names with the court: Hasan, Harar, Shadianman, Hadilan, Saolan, Yikeli, Balihei, Anlima, Tuohuma, Chalishi, Ganshi, Buhala, Pala, Nishawuer, Kashmir, Tiebili, Huotan, Huozhan, Kuxian, Yaxi, Yargan, Rong, Bai, Wulun, Aduan, Yesicheng, Shehei, Baiyin, and Kefu—twenty-nine districts in all.

sentences.zh: 以疆域褊小，止稱地面。

translations.literal: Because their territories are narrow and small, they only style themselves ground districts.
translations.idiomatic: Their domains were small and they styled themselves only local districts.

sentences.zh: 與哈烈、哈實哈兒、賽藍、亦力把力、失剌思、沙鹿海牙、阿速、把丹皆由哈密入嘉峪關，或三年、五年一貢，入京者不得過三十五人。

translations.literal: Together with Herat, Kashgar, Sayram, Yarkand, Shiraz, Sarai, Asud, and Badan—all enter through Hami at Jiayu Pass; tribute may be every three or five years; those entering the capital may not exceed thirty-five persons.
translations.idiomatic: Herat, Kashgar, Sayram, Yarkand, Shiraz, Sarai, Asud, and Badan all entered through Hami at Jiayu Pass, sending tribute every three or five years with no more than thirty-five men allowed into the capital.

sentences.zh: 其不由哈密者，更有乞兒、麻米兒、哈蘭可脫、蠟燭、也的幹、剌竹、亦不剌、因格失、迷乞兒、吉思羽奴、思哈辛十一地面，亦嘗通貢。

translations.literal: Those not passing through Hami further include eleven ground districts: Qier, Mamier, Halan Ketuo, Fula Zhula, Yedigan, Lazhu, Yibula, Yingeshi, Miqier, Jisiyunu, and Sihaxin—they also once communicated tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Those not routed through Hami included eleven further districts—Qier, Mamier, Halan Ketuo, Fula Zhula, Yedigan, Lazhu, Yibula, Yingeshi, Miqier, Jisiyunu, and Sihaxin—which had also sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 附 魯迷

translations.literal: Appendix: Rum
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Rum

sentences.zh: 魯迷，去中國絕遠。

translations.literal: Rum is extremely distant from China.
translations.idiomatic: Rum lay at the farthest remove from China.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年遣使貢獅子、西牛。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing it sent envoys presenting lions and western oxen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jiajing it sent envoys with lions and western oxen.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄭一鵬言：「魯迷非嘗貢之邦，獅子非可育之獸，請卻之，以光聖德。」

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zheng Yipeng said: 'Rum is not a state that has regularly offered tribute; lions are not beasts that can be reared—please refuse them to glorify sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zheng Yipeng said, "Rum is not a regular tributary state, and lions are not animals that can be kept in captivity—please refuse them to display sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 禮官席書等言：「魯迷不列《王會》，其真偽不可知。

translations.literal: Rites officials Xi Shu and others said: 'Rum is not listed in the Royal Assembly; its authenticity cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Rites officials Xi Shu and others said, "Rum does not appear in the Royal Assembly; its authenticity is unknown.

sentences.zh: 近土魯番數侵甘肅，而邊吏于魯迷冊內，察有土魯番之人。

translations.literal: Recently Turfan has repeatedly raided Gansu, yet border officials in Rum's register detected people of Turfan.
translations.idiomatic: Turfan had lately raided Gansu repeatedly, yet border officials found Turfan natives listed on Rum's register.

sentences.zh: 其狡詐明甚，請遣之出關，治所獲間諜罪。」

translations.literal: Their cunning and deceit are clearly evident—please send them out of the pass and punish the spies captured.'
translations.idiomatic: Their fraud was plain—send them beyond the pass and punish the spies seized."

sentences.zh: 帝竟納之，而令邊臣察治。

translations.literal: The emperor nevertheless accepted them, and ordered border officials to investigate and handle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nevertheless accepted the gifts and ordered frontier officials to investigate.

sentences.zh: 五年冬，復以二物來貢。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year they again came with the two creatures to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year they again presented the two animals as tribute.

sentences.zh: 既頒賜，其使臣言，長途跋涉，費至二萬二千余金，請加賜。

translations.literal: After rewards were granted, their envoys said that the long journey had cost more than twenty-two thousand in gold and requested additional gifts.
translations.idiomatic: After rewards were issued, the envoys said the long journey had cost more than twenty-two thousand taels of gold and asked for added compensation.

sentences.zh: 御史張祿言：「華夷異方，人物異性，留人養畜，不惟違物，抑且拂人。

translations.literal: Censor Zhang Lu said: 'China and the barbarians are different realms; people and things have different natures—keeping men to rear beasts not only violates creatures but also offends human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhang Lu said, "China and foreign lands differ; men and beasts differ in nature—keeping men to feed animals offends both creatures and human decency.

sentences.zh: 況養獅日用二羊，養西牛日用果餌。

translations.literal: Moreover rearing a lion consumes two sheep daily; rearing a western ox consumes fruit fodder daily.
translations.idiomatic: A lion required two sheep a day; a western ox required daily fruit feed.

sentences.zh: 獸相食與食人食，聖賢皆惡之。

translations.literal: Beasts eating one another and eating human food—sages all detest this.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts devouring one another and consuming food meant for people—sages condemned both.

sentences.zh: 又調禦人役，日需供億。

translations.literal: Again conscripting imperial attendants, daily supplies are required in vast amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants were conscripted and supplies demanded daily without end.

sentences.zh: 以光祿有限之財，充人獸無益之費，殊為拂經。

translations.literal: Using the limited wealth of the Court of Imperial Entertainments to fill useless expenses for men and beasts greatly violates principle.
translations.idiomatic: To spend the Court of Imperial Entertainments' limited funds on useless costs for men and beasts was deeply contrary to principle.

sentences.zh: 乞返其人，卻其物，薄其賞，明中國聖人不貴異物之意。」

translations.literal: I beg to return their people, refuse their goods, reduce their rewards, and make clear that China's sages do not prize strange objects.
translations.idiomatic: Return their men, refuse the animals, reduce their rewards, and show that China's sages do not prize exotic things.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: This was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 乃從禮官言，如弘治撒馬兒罕例益之。

translations.literal: Thereupon following the rites officials' words, they increased gifts as in the Hongzhi precedent for Samarkand.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the court followed the rites officials and increased gifts as under the Hongzhi precedent for Samarkand.

sentences.zh: 二十二年偕天方諸國貢馬及方物，明年還至甘州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year together with Mecca and various states they presented horses and local products; the next year returning they reached Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year they presented horses and regional goods together with Mecca and other states; the following year, on their return, they reached Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 會迤北賊入寇，總兵官楊信令貢使九十餘人往禦，死者九人。

translations.literal: It happened that northern raiders invaded; Regional Commander Yang Xin ordered more than ninety tribute envoys to go defend; nine died.
translations.idiomatic: When northern raiders invaded, Regional Commander Yang Xin sent more than ninety tribute envoys to fight; nine were killed.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，褫信職，命有司棺斂歸其喪。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he stripped Xin of his post and ordered the authorities to coffin and bury them and return their remains.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing this, the emperor stripped Yang Xin of his post and ordered officials to coffin the dead and return their remains.

sentences.zh: 二十七年、三十三年併入貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh and thirty-third years they joined in tribute together.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh and thirty-third years they sent joint tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 其貢物有珊瑚、琥珀、金剛鑽、花瓷器、鎖服、撒哈剌帳、羚羊角、西狗皮、舍列猻皮、鐵角皮之屬。

translations.literal: Their tribute goods include coral, amber, diamonds, flowered porcelain, chain-mail garments, Saharan tents, antelope horns, western dog pelts, jackal pelts, rhinoceros horn, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Their tribute included coral, amber, diamonds, decorated porcelain, mail armor, Saharan tents, antelope horn, western dog pelts, jackal pelts, rhinoceros horn, and the like.
